_comment: Notification-hook surface: every priority critical|high entry whose last_changed_at falls in the last 7 days, most recently changed first. last_changed_at = max(discovered_at, every non-internal updates[].at): it moves on a new finding AND on every reader-facing update, correction or improvement (updated_at moves only on a type:update record). Poll this file and alert on a new `id` OR a changed `last_changed_at` for a known id. `immediate_action` is non-null exactly when priority is critical. URLs are absolute (`url` == `permalink`; `markdown_url` is the entry's raw Markdown source). Schema: {id, url, permalink, markdown_url, priority, kind, headline, summary, discovered_at, updated_at|null, last_changed_at, updates[{at,type,summary}], immediate_action:{title,action}|null, actions[], exploited, kev, cve_ids[], cves[{id,cvss|null,status[],affected|null,fixed|null}], affected_products[], entities[], techniques[], tags[], sectors[], regions[], verification, classification|null, org_triage:{category,rationale}|null}. exploited = an exploitation tag or a CVE status of exploited/cisa-kev; kev = a CVE on the CISA KEV list. techniques[] carries the entry's MITRE ATT&CK ids (frontmatter + prose-derived, revoked ids resolved forward); classification is the collapsed Admiralty code (e.g. B2). For the do-now task list of every priority, poll data/actions.json. See docs/pipeline.md.

actions: Upgrade every Zimbra Collaboration host to 10.1.21 (10.1.20 is the minimum for CVE-2026-73570); where the upgrade cannot happen at once, remove the zimbra-snmp package or disable SNMP notifications and restrict SNMP and SMTP to trusted hosts.

On every host that ran a build before 10.1.20 with SNMP notifications enabled at any time since 2026-07-28, upgrading is not enough: rotate all domain zimbraPreAuthKey values and run the compromise check on every mailbox node, covering the zimbra user's crontab and /opt/zimbra/.ssh/authorized_keys, JSP or stray text files under /opt/zimbra/jetty_base/webapps/zimbra/public, droppers in /tmp and /var/tmp, and outbound connections from the mail server; where web shells or an LDAP dump turn up, rotate every mailbox and administrative credential.

cves.affected: Zimbra Collaboration before 10.1.20, where the optional zimbra-snmp package is installed and SNMP notifications are enabled

alerts.headline: Fixed on 20 July, identified on 13 August, probed from 28 July: a CVE-keyed patch process never saw this one coming
alerts.summary: Zimbra shipped ZCS 10.1.20 on 2026-07-20 with a fix for a command injection in the SNMP monitoring component, and the identifier CVE-2026-73570 followed on 2026-08-13. Microsoft Threat Intelligence now reports confirmed intrusions in more than one region and industry, with probing of the injection point from 2026-07-28, before disclosure, and CISA lists the flaw in KEV (added 2026-08-21). The flaw needs no authentication and applies only where the optional zimbra-snmp package is installed and SNMP notifications are enabled; Microsoft's cases combined web shells, root escalation, theft of Zimbra's authentication keys and cluster-wide movement, so an upgrade does not evict an attacker already inside. CSIRT Italia reports that exploitation of this flaw has also led to ELock-family ransomware, cryptomining and theft of the LDAP database and credential hashes on exposed servers, and found no intrusion on regularly updated instances.

updates.summary: Microsoft Threat Intelligence published first-hand analysis of confirmed intrusions: probing of the injection point from 2026-07-28, before the 2026-08-13 disclosure, then web shells, root escalation, theft of Zimbra's authentication keys and cluster-wide movement, with the injection signature to hunt for. The 10.1.21 release, which also fixes unauthenticated password-recovery code prediction, and NCSC-CH's advisory of 2026-10-01 are added. CISA's KEV listing of 2026-08-21, not recorded before, is added; the 10.1.20 release date is corrected to 2026-07-20, the EPSS score is refreshed to 0.117 (FIRST, 2026-10-01), ENISA's 18 August date is its EU KEV listing, and the actions now ask for a compromise check as well as the upgrade.

CSIRT Italia's bulletin of 2026-10-05 reports compromises of exposed Zimbra servers through CVE-2026-73570 that ended in ELock-family ransomware, cryptomining, web shells with theft of the LDAP database and credential hashes, and a 48-hour mail outage for more than 6,000 mailboxes, and found no intrusion on regularly updated instances. Its host checks (the zimbra user's crontab and authorized_keys, JSP files in the Jetty public directory, droppers in temporary directories, egress) are added to the compromise check.

Elastic Security Labs reproduced the chain and found that several public proofs of concept never trigger it, so a failed test does not show a host is patched; its process-lineage detection for the Swatchdog notification path is added to the detection guidance.

actions: On every WordPress site your organisation, its web agencies or its hosting suppliers run with UpdraftPlus, free or premium, including old municipal, campaign and project sites, check for an UpdraftCentral key (wp option get updraft_central_localkeys, or Settings > UpdraftPlus Backups > Advanced Tools > UpdraftCentral) and delete every key even if nobody remembers using UpdraftCentral, then update to 1.26.13 or 2.26.13 or later; deleting a key stops remote management only, and backups keep working.

On any site where a plugin, must-use plugin or Editor account holding manage_options appears that nobody created, delete the UpdraftCentral key first, then restore the site from a backup taken before 17 October, rotate every administrator and UpdraftCentral password, the teamupdraft.com account password (which UpdraftPlus Premium can leave stored in the site database and its backups) and end all sessions.
alerts.headline: Stolen UpdraftCentral keys install backdoor plugins on WordPress sites; the plugin update alone does not evict them
alerts.summary: TeamUpdraft, the vendor of the UpdraftPlus backup plugin, says unauthorised access to teamupdraft.com on 17 and 18 October probably exposed its customer database, including UpdraftCentral connection keys, and Patchstack and Nethemba report an attacker using those keys to install backdoor plugins on connected WordPress sites, which Patchstack's telemetry dates from 2026-10-18 15:32 (it gives no time zone), and that create hidden administrators. It is not a flaw in UpdraftPlus: the plugin obeys commands signed with a valid key, a key exists on many sites that never used the service because connecting a teamupdraft.com account ticks the option by default, and the update disconnects only connections made before 13:07 BST (12:07 UTC) on 18 October, so keys created later that day have to be deleted by hand. TeamUpdraft says the attacker used a compromised key to enter its own site, and Nethemba saw the stolen keys used again on 2026-10-21, after 1.26.13 shipped.

updates.summary: TeamUpdraft says the attacker entered its site with a compromised key and suspects AI-accelerated tooling, and asks users to check the sites listed in their UpdraftCentral account; Nethemba saw the stolen keys used again on 2026-10-21 after 1.26.13 shipped and reads UpdraftPlus Premium as leaving the account password stored in the site database and backups.

actions: Tell the helpdesk, HR and payroll teams of every body whose staff are insured with Publica (including the federal administration and the ETH domain) or with the Pensionskasse Stadt Zürich, which says data of its insured persons and pensioners was stolen, that AHV number, date of birth, address, salary and IBAN may now be known to criminals and must not count as proof of identity, and route requests that quote them, a request to change a payout account included, to a call-back on a known number; for staff insured with Pensionskasse Post, the Bernische Pensionskasse (which now says it must be assumed personal data left), the Ticino cantonal fund IPCT (which found data of about 1,800 of its insured persons on the attacked server and writes to all its insured because it cannot exclude more), a fund administered or advised by Libera AG or the Bernische Lehrerversicherungskasse apply the same rule until those funds report the scope; also tell insured staff that cantonal police warn of investment-fraud calls from people who know their salary and pension details, which prove nothing about the caller.

If your organisation's pension administration, HR or payroll runs on PK Softech software, is being migrated to it or tested on it, or your staff are insured with Pensionskasse Post, ask the supplier or the fund in writing whether your data, test data included, was in the affected environment, project, test and migration copies included, and what it holds outside the productive system.
alerts.headline: PK Softech apparently kept Publica data it had promised in writing to delete; Tamedia says Akira holds about 100 GB
alerts.summary: PK Softech AG, the software supplier of Publica and other Swiss pension funds, says unknown attackers used malware to reach part of its IT and that data must be assumed to have left; the Confederation headlined its 2026-10-08 release "data outflow confirmed", and the Federal Prosecutor's Office is investigating. Tamedia reports that PK Softech had confirmed in writing in January 2026 that it deleted Publica's 2019 migration data, which apparently stayed on its servers, and that Akira holds about 100 GB and demands ransom; Inside IT relays this and adds that the Federal Prosecutor's Office confirmed Akira took data, and Netzwoche relays that the authorities assume data on practically all current and former federal and federally affiliated staff left. Publica says personal data of insured persons has presumably left; the Pensionskasse Stadt Zürich says its insured persons' test data was stolen, the Pensionskasse Post says personal data left, the Bernische Pensionskasse says it must be assumed so, the Ticino fund IPCT says data of about 1,800 of its insured persons sat on the attacked server and writes to all its insured because it cannot exclude more, and other funds are still checking. As of 2026-10-22 neither the Confederation nor Publica has itself named the actor or the demand.

updates.summary: The supplier's customers are now named: the Bernische Pensionskasse (canton of Bern staff and three cantonal universities) says its supplier is the same company that serves Publica, the Bernische Lehrerversicherungskasse and Pensionskasse Post report the supplier incident, and Inside IT lists Migros-Pensionskasse and Syngenta Pensionskasse among the customers. None of the funds has confirmed which member data left.

Publica's own page of 2026-10-08 lists civil status and the IBAN among the data that could be affected and says its investigation indicates personal data of insured persons has presumably left. The AWP agency relays the software firm's position that it knows data left but not yet whether personal data is among it, that it may be business data, and that the volume is rather small.

The Pensionskasse Stadt Zürich, the City of Zurich's pension fund, says on 2026-10-13 that it currently uses another provider, plans to move to PK Softech's system in early 2027 and is checking whether data from migration tests was affected. Publica's page says as of 2026-10-14 that it has no indications that data from the attack was published on the darkweb.

Cantonal police warn that criminals could use the leaked salary and pension data to phone insured persons with investment-fraud offers, SwissCybersecurity.net ties the warning to PK Softech, and the Zurich cantonal fund BVK says its PK Softech software runs in its own data centre so it is not directly affected; PK Softech can neither confirm nor rule out further affected customers, and the Ticino fund listed as a customer has made no statement.

The Pensionskasse Stadt Zürich, the City of Zurich's pension fund, now says in its notice of 2026-10-15 that its inquiries indicate personal data of its insured persons and pensioners, handed to PK Softech as test data for a planned 2027 switch, was stolen, and that which fields were taken is still being clarified. Pensionskasse Post says in its notice of the same date that personal data did leave and no longer repeats its earlier anonymisation statement, though it is still unclear whether its insured persons' data is among it.

SonntagsBlick reports, from a confidential federal information note, that the Confederation rates the incident as serious and says the security organs of the Confederation are particularly affected, which it glosses as the Federal Intelligence Service, the Defence Group and fedpol, that the Federal Council was briefed on 2026-10-14 and that the cantons were informed; the Finance Department confirms only the briefing. NZZ adds that the pension consultancy Libera AG is also affected, that the Bernische Pensionskasse now says it must be assumed personal data left, and that Publica ran no regular on-site audits at the supplier.

Tamedia reports, and Inside IT relays, that the Akira ransomware group holds about 100 GB of the pension data of well over 100,000 current and former federal employees, with employer details of staff under cover identity among it, and demands ransom; neither the Confederation nor Publica confirms the actor or the demand.

Netzwoche, relaying Tages-Anzeiger, reports that the Federal Council and the security authorities now assume data on practically all current and former federal and federally affiliated staff left, federal judges and former Federal Council members among them, and that an on-site inspection at PK Softech on 2026-10-07 established the outflow of security-relevant data; neither the Confederation nor Publica has confirmed the actor, the demand or the scope.

The supplier's written pledge to delete Publica's 2019 migration data was apparently not kept, Inside IT relays that the Federal Prosecutor's Office confirmed Akira exfiltrated data, though that is second-hand and neither the Confederation nor Publica has itself named the actor, and the Ticino cantonal fund IPCT says all its insured could potentially be involved but has no evidence yet that data was taken.

The Ticino cantonal fund IPCT says in a letter of 2026-10-23 that data of about 1,800 of its insured persons (about 1,700 who left in 2024 and 2025, with exit-benefit amounts and IBANs, and about 80 on disability pensions) sat on the attacked supplier server for two ongoing projects; it has no certain evidence the data were taken but finds it plausible, and it writes to all insured because it cannot exclude more.

actions: Update the PHP runtime, not the CMS or its plugins, on every internet-facing server and container image to 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 or 8.2.35 or to your distribution's patched package, restart PHP-FPM, Apache and every long-running worker, rebuild images, and confirm the running version, because a distribution backport can keep the old version string; isolate any application that cannot be updated from public networks until it is.

After updating, set session.upload_progress.enabled=0 on every PHP host and keep it there until PHP's next regular bugfix release: CVE-2026-115560, which the October releases do not fix, needs session upload progress to be enabled.

immediate_action.action: Two unauthenticated remote-code-execution flaws in PHP itself are being scanned for and attacked, fixed builds (8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, 8.2.35) have been out since 2026-10-21, and public proofs of concept circulate. Update PHP, not the CMS, on every internet-facing server and container image, restart PHP-FPM, Apache and all long-running workers, and confirm the running version, because distribution packages can keep the old version string. Isolate anything that cannot be updated from public networks, and check web roots, logs, crashes and unexpected processes, since an update does not remove an attacker who is already in.

alerts.summary: The PHP project released 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35 on 2026-10-21 to fix CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 (CVSS 4.0 9.2), two flaws in the runtime itself that allow unauthenticated remote code execution as the web worker account, most directly on Apache mod_php; PHP 8.1 and older get no upstream release. Attack traffic is reported and public proofs of concept circulate: Palo Alto Networks' Unit 42 reports a confirmed intrusion of a European government entity with agentic post-exploitation, from its own telemetry and without naming the victim or the flaw that gave the foothold, while CrowdStrike, Sophos and Wordfence report no successful exploitation, and VulnCheck holds a working exploit for PHP 8.4.10 to 8.4.26 and 8.5.10 to 8.5.11 on mod_php. PHP also published an informational advisory for a third code-execution path, CVE-2026-115560, that the October releases do not fix: keep session.upload_progress.enabled=0 until the next regular release. BACS knows of no attack in Switzerland but says PHP applications of the federal administration were affected and that it has no complete overview of the update status; Swiss cantons, universities, the host Cyon with more than 100,000 sites, the Lodur fire-brigade platform and Publica took sites offline as a precaution.

updates.summary: The fixed releases (PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35) shipped on 2026-10-21, so the earlier no-fix status ends; Cloudflare, watchTowr and VulnCheck report attack traffic and at least one unsuccessful web-shell attempt, proofs of concept are circulating, VulnCheck holds an exploit that succeeds with ASLR enabled and no source reports a confirmed compromise, so priority moves to critical. Swiss cantons, universities, the Lodur fire-brigade platform and Publica took sites offline as a precaution, and BACS, CERT-EU and ENISA tell operators to update the runtime, check embedded installations and look for compromise.

BACS says it knows of no attack in Switzerland but that PHP applications of the federal administration were affected and that it has no complete overview of the update status; the host Cyon took more than 100,000 sites offline for hours, a UK minister reports 32 government services unavailable with no confirmed compromise, and AWS reports a first exploit attempt on 2026-10-17. Sansec and Red Hat judge exploitation harder than VulnCheck's exploit suggests, and Palo Alto now schedules PAN-OS hotfixes for 2026-10-26 to 2026-10-30.

Unit 42 reports a confirmed intrusion of a European government entity with agentic post-exploitation, from its own telemetry and without naming the victim or the flaw that gave the foothold, while CrowdStrike, Sophos and Wordfence report no successful exploitation; PHP adds an informational advisory for a third code-execution path, CVE-2026-115560, that the October releases do not fix, and advises session.upload_progress.enabled=0 until its next regular release. VulnCheck's exploit now covers PHP 8.5.10 and 8.5.11 as well as 8.4.10 to 8.4.26, and Cisco, Splunk and Palo Alto Networks revised their product statuses.

alerts.headline: Arista confirms exploitation of a VeloCloud Orchestrator flaw: any tenant login, even read-only, reaches operator rights

actions: In every Entra tenant you or your MSP administer, disable without deleting the seven ConnectWise application identities that ConnectWise lists by client ID (Cloud Backup is 506e08f9-6e9a-4da4-942b-a099a03644ae; the other six are in ConnectWise's advisory), dormant connections included, and keep them disabled until ConnectWise gives restoration instructions; where Graph activity logs were enabled, review them for these apps until at least 90 minutes after you disabled them, because a token issued before the disable stays valid for up to 90 minutes, and preserve the sign-in and audit logs promptly without delaying containment, because Entra ID Free keeps only 7 days.
In the same tenants list the apps owned by the ConnectWise S-K LLC tenant (3f9cd7a0-127a-4ed4-bf06-2f830d5616b7), and disable each that you do not use or cannot verify as safe.

In the same tenants review every enterprise application and app registration, MSP management and security tools first but none skipped (Huntress saw the secrets planted on apparently random applications, in one tenant on some of the least privileged ones), for client secrets, certificates and federated credentials added since 2026-10-13 and remove any you did not create; also check the directory roles, owners and consent grants held by ConnectWise and SkyKick service principals, Conditional Access exclusions for them, and mailbox forwarding, inbox and transport rules and delegated access, because disabling the vendor applications does not remove access planted through them.
alerts.headline: ConnectWise SkyKick app credential used in 162+ Microsoft 365 tenants; disabling it does not undo planted access
alerts.summary: ConnectWise says it identified unauthorized access to application identities of its Cloud Backup (formerly SkyKick) service; Huntress and Todyl report that from 15 October the app's credential was used to obtain app-only Microsoft Graph tokens in customer Microsoft 365 tenants; Huntress alone confirmed unauthorized sign-ins in 162 tenants by 16 October and saw ConnectWise Cloud Management apps assign themselves directory roles in about 50 tenants and, in two tenants, a scripted Global Administrator self-grant followed by new client secrets planted on apparently random applications. ConnectWise disabled seven application identities and suspended the service on 17 October, but says disabling does not reverse changes already made in a tenant, so every tenant that ever consented a ConnectWise or SkyKick app needs the apps disabled and its application credentials, directory roles and consents reviewed. Microsoft assesses that the China-state aligned actor Storm-0940 is behind it, using the ARTEX agentic-AI framework, and says it attempted sign-ins to more than 2,250 tenants; how the credential was obtained and what data was read are not public.

updates.summary: ConnectWise's update of 2026-10-18 01:00 UTC took SaaS Security and Cloud Management offline in addition to Cloud Backup, which had been suspended since 2026-10-17, so its monitoring and alerting is out of service, and its latest update (2026-10-19 01:15 UTC) gives no restoration time; Todyl and SpecterOps say a token issued before an app is disabled stays valid for up to 90 minutes, and ConnectWise says previously issued tokens may remain usable until they expire; and Todyl says to find every SkyKick and ConnectWise app in a tenant, inherited ones included, while Todyl and SpecterOps point to the apps owned by ConnectWise's vendor tenant.

Huntress's update of 2026-10-19 reports a second tenant with scripted post-compromise activity (the application granting itself Global Administrator and planting a secret on other applications, the choice of applications apparently random), bounds the sign-in activity to the morning of 2026-10-15 UTC with the last successful sign-in at 08:44 UTC, and says Graph directory reads leave no audit record; the secret check therefore has to cover every application.

Sophos X-Ops reports the same token sweep from its own telemetry, from a single server in ascending tenant order and including tenants with no active backup subscription, and found no planted secrets, applications, consents or role assignments in the tenants it reviewed, unlike Huntress's two tenants.

Microsoft Threat Intelligence assesses that Storm-0940, a China-state aligned actor, was responsible for the compromise, using the ARTEX agentic-AI framework to attempt sign-ins to more than 2,250 tenants after an automated password spray from the same network range, and warns that credential changes planted in tenants can persist after the vendor application is remediated. ConnectWise itself says it appears a China state-aligned group was responsible and began restoring services in controlled phases on 2026-10-21.

alerts.headline: Exim 4.99.3 fixes an unauthenticated use-after-free in BDAT handling on GnuTLS builds (CVE-2026-45185)
alerts.summary: Exim 4.99.3, released on 2026-05-12, fixes CVE-2026-45185 (CVSS 9.8), a remotely reachable use-after-free in the GnuTLS backend: a client that sends a TLS close_notify before a BDAT body is complete and then one cleartext byte makes Exim write into its freed TLS transfer buffer, corrupting the heap. It affects Exim 4.97 to 4.99.2 built with GnuTLS that advertise STARTTLS and CHUNKING; GnuTLS is the default TLS library on many Debian-based distributions including Ubuntu, and the only mitigation is the upgrade.

updates.summary: The exploits produced with an LLM during the disclosure window worked only against non-PIE builds, first without and then with ASLR; against the default PIE build no full exploit was reported, the researcher's side getting as far as a leaked stack address. The Exim maintainers know no mitigation other than upgrading to 4.99.3, so disabling CHUNKING advertisement is not a vendor workaround, and the advisory sets the CVSS 9.8 and the affected range of 4.97 to 4.99.2 on builds with GnuTLS.

alerts.summary: Fortinet's advisories of 2026-05-12 fix CVE-2026-44277, improper access control on FortiAuthenticator API endpoints, and CVE-2026-26083, missing authorization in the FortiSandbox, FortiSandbox Cloud and FortiSandbox PaaS web UI; both let an unauthenticated attacker execute unauthorized code or commands through crafted requests (CVSSv3 9.8 base, 9.1 temporal). alerts.headline: ESET: China-aligned Webworm targeted governments in Belgium, Italy, Serbia and Poland with Discord and OneDrive implants
alerts.summary: ESET reported on 2026-05-20 that the China-aligned group Webworm targeted governmental organizations in Belgium, Italy, Serbia and Poland, and a South African university, in 2025 with two new backdoors: EchoCreep, written in Go, which takes commands through Discord, and GraphWorm, which uses Microsoft Graph and OneDrive for command and control. A compromised third-party Amazon S3 bucket held its proxy configurations and files taken from Italian and Spanish governmental entities; ESET could not find the entry point, but the group scanned victims' web servers and ran a public SquirrelMail exploit (CVE-2017-7692) against a Serbian webmail target.

updates.summary: ESET links Webworm to SixLittleMonkeys and FishMonger as related groups and calls a Space Pirates link tenuous, so none of them are names for Webworm; EchoCreep reports to Discord channels the operators created in advance rather than creating them. The S3 bucket was a compromised third-party bucket, since taken down, and SharpSecretsdump was only uploaded to it.

alerts.headline: Tycoon 2FA adds device-code phishing: victims approve token issuance to an attacker device on genuine Microsoft pages
alerts.summary: eSentire reported on 2026-05-12 a late-April 2026 campaign in which Tycoon 2FA operators, still active after the March 2026 takedown, added an OAuth device-code variant alongside their credential-relay kit: an invoice lure with a Trustifi click-tracking link leads through Cloudflare Workers and encrypted JavaScript layers to a fake Microsoft CAPTCHA and a voicemail page showing a device code the operator's backend obtained. The victim pastes it at microsoft.com/devicelogin, signs in and approves MFA on genuine Microsoft infrastructure, and Microsoft issues Microsoft Authentication Broker tokens to the operator's polling client; eSentire's hunts look for device-code sign-ins and Node.js user agents in Entra ID logs.

updates.summary: Tycoon 2FA operators added an OAuth device-code variant alongside the credential-relay kit rather than abandoning it, and the Alibaba (US) hosting eSentire saw since about 2026-04-10 joins the previously documented providers instead of replacing them. The lure shows a device code fetched by the operator's backend and has the victim paste it at microsoft.com/devicelogin; the detection signals are eSentire's own (successful deviceCode sign-ins from sources with no prior device-code use, the Microsoft Authentication Broker AppId, node or undici user agents, ResultType 50173 after revocation). eSentire's hardening leads with a Conditional Access block on the device-code flow, and no source says that FIDO2 sign-in defeats device-code phishing.

alerts.headline: Leaked chats of The Gentlemen ransomware group show its edge-device access, NTLM relay and EDR-kill toolkit
alerts.summary: The Gentlemen ransomware-as-a-service administrator acknowledged on 2026-05-04 that the group's internal Rocket backend had leaked, and Check Point Research analysed a 44.4 MB part of a leak a seller's screenshot put at about 16.22 GB. The chats show access through Fortinet and Cisco edge devices by brute force, known vulnerabilities and bought access, NTLM relay and certificate-services abuse, tools that block EDR at start-up, ZeroPulse and Velociraptor for remote access and Cloudflare tunnels for persistence; Check Point counts about 332 leak-site victims in the first five months of 2026. A free decryptor released in April recovers files only from a memory image of the ransomware process captured while it was running.

updates.summary: The free Gentlemen decryptor released in April 2026 recovers files only from a memory image of the ransomware process captured while it ran, has no master key and predates the leak, so trying decryption before negotiating does not help most victims; capturing the running locker's memory does. The 1,570 figure is victims of one affiliate's SystemBC server from an earlier Check Point investigation, not hidden ransomware victims, and the group tracks CVE-2024-55591 among other CVEs without the chats showing exploitation. Initial access usually runs through Fortinet and Cisco edge devices by brute force, known vulnerabilities and bought access, the ETW and NTDLL tampering belongs to the locker, and the 8,200 chat lines are DynaRisk's count.

alerts.headline: Storm-2949 hijacked privileged Entra ID accounts through SSPR abuse, then mined Azure management features for data
alerts.summary: Microsoft Threat Intelligence reported on 2026-05-18 that Storm-2949 abused Microsoft's Self-Service Password Reset to take over four privileged Entra ID accounts at one organization, re-enrolled MFA on its own devices, and used their Azure RBAC roles to pull App Service publishing profiles, Key Vault secrets, SQL and Storage data and VM access through Run Command and VMAccess. The actor relied mostly on legitimate cloud management features, installed ScreenConnect on VMs, aimed at mass data exfiltration and, per Microsoft, did not extort and shows no link to ShinyHunters.

updates.summary: Microsoft does not call Storm-2949 financially motivated: its objective was mass data exfiltration, Storm is a temporary designation, no extortion was seen and there is no ShinyHunters link, and the intrusion was not binary-free, since ScreenConnect was installed on VMs, where a script tried to weaken Defender and to clear event logs. Self-service password reset abuse took over four privileged accounts on a hedged phishing assessment.

alerts.summary: CVE-2026-41091 (CVSS 7.8) is a link-following flaw in the Microsoft Malware Protection Engine that lets an authorized local attacker gain SYSTEM, and CVE-2026-45498 (CVSS 3.1 base score 4.0) is a denial of service in the Microsoft Defender Antimalware Platform. updates.summary: UPDATE (originally covered 2026-05-20): Both Microsoft Defender vulnerabilities confirmed as actively exploited in the wild in a combined out-of-band engine update (The Hacker News, 2026-05-21).

CVE-2026-41091 is fixed in Malware Protection Engine version 1.1.26040.8 and CVE-2026-45498, a denial of service rather than a privilege escalation, in Antimalware Platform version 4.18.26040.7: two separate updates, not one out-of-band release. alerts.headline: Dirty Frag: two kernel page-cache write flaws give local root; Microsoft saw su escalation that may be it or Copy Fail
alerts.summary: Dirty Frag is two Linux kernel flaws, CVE-2026-43284 in the xfrm-ESP receive path and CVE-2026-43500 in RxRPC, that let a local user write into the page cache of read-only files and gain root deterministically. A public exploit appeared on 2026-05-07, mainline and distribution fixes are released, and Microsoft reports limited su-based escalation in the wild that may be Dirty Frag or Copy Fail.

updates.summary: Dirty Frag Linux LPE now confirmed exploited in the wild; Microsoft Threat Intelligence reports "limited in-the-wild activity" involving su privilege escalation after SSH initial access (Microsoft Security Blog, 2026-05-08). Red Hat published RHSB-2026-003 with backports rolling out (Red Hat, updated 2026-05-09); NCSC.ch issued a Swiss federal advisory (NCSC-CH Security Hub post 12547, 2026-05-08).

A related follow-on flaw, CVE-2026-46300 ("Fragnesia", tracked in its own entry), reopens this vulnerability's page-cache-write primitive on hosts patched only against CVE-2026-43284: a 13-year-old bug in the kernel's skb-coalescing code drops the shared-fragment marker the original fix relies on. Public Kubernetes-context proof-of-concept exploits now exist, and Red Hat confirms RHEL kernels need the CVE-2026-46300 fix too. EPSS scores (FIRST.org, 2026-09-04) are now populated: 0.9324 for CVE-2026-43284 and 0.9286 for CVE-2026-43500.

Exploitation of Dirty Frag is not confirmed: Microsoft's observation may be Dirty Frag or Copy Fail, and Microsoft does not report exfiltration, so the exploited status is removed. The root cause is in-place decryption of a spliced page-cache page, not DMA remapping; only the ESP variant needs a user namespace; the tested distributions and Ubuntu releases were wrong; Red Hat's bulletin does not cover CVE-2026-43500, which does not affect Red Hat, and its targeted sysctl is user.max_user_namespaces; a file-write watch cannot see the page-cache write; and Microsoft does not mention AIDE, IMA or auditd. The summary's pending-patch state is superseded: both mainline fixes and distribution kernels are released. CVSS for CVE-2026-43284 is the CNA's 8.8, the duplicate Red Hat source and self-quoted evidence are removed, and the earlier sections are corrected in place. The two flaws' write primitives are told apart (4 chosen bytes into a setuid binary for ESP, 8 brute-forced bytes into /etc/passwd for RxRPC), the Copy Fail CVE is cited to Microsoft, the on-disk clause to Aikido, the AFS effect to Ubuntu, the 2013 bug is described without a function name the sources do not give, the NCSC-CH citation points at the public hub post, and the action is cut to the patch task. The main analysis gains Exposure and takeaway lines.

FIRST's EPSS scores are refreshed to 2026-10-20: CVE-2026-43500 has fallen to 0.0262 from 0.9286 on 2026-09-04, while CVE-2026-43284 stands at 0.9419. Microsoft's report is credited to its Defender Security Research Team, which wrote it. Red Hat's 'Copy Fail 2' nickname is dropped from the main analysis, and the separate Copy Fail entry (CVE-2026-31431) is linked.

alerts.headline: A netadmin user on Cisco SD-WAN can become root through a crafted upload file; Mandiant saw zero-day use in April
alerts.summary: CVE-2026-20245 (CVSS 7.8) lets an authenticated attacker with netadmin privileges on Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Controller, Manager or Validator execute commands as root through a crafted file. Mandiant reconstructed its zero-day use in April 2026 at a service provider, after rogue peering access; CISA added it to its KEV catalog on 2026-06-09, and fixed releases exist for every supported train.

updates.summary: Mandiant reconstructs a months-long zero-day compromise of Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager (CVE-2026-20245), updating our 6 June coverage, GTIG details an authenticated request tenant-upload CLI command-injection path that planted a troot UID-0 account on the controller, reached after a peering-auth-bypass foothold and exploited at a service provider from late 2025 through March 2026, well before the patch (Mandiant/GTIG, 2026-06-24). UPDATE (originally covered 2026-06-26): Google Mandiant (GTIG) published (2026-06-24) the first complete TTP chain for the Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager zero-day activity, observed at a service-provider victim from late 2025 into 2026 (Google Mandiant, 2026-06-24).

The title, summary, body and action still said no patch existed, although fixed releases shipped from 2026-06-09 and Cisco added a Live Protect shield. CVE-2026-20245 was typed as an unauthenticated bypass with no score; it is an authenticated local netadmin-to-root flaw scored 7.8, and the companion CVE-2026-20182 scores 10.0. Mandiant dates the zero-day exploitation to April 2026 at a service provider, not late 2025 to March at a communications provider; it presents the peering-bypass foothold as a possibility, and reports file deletion and configuration rollback rather than history or syslog deletion. The entry is rewritten with the Controller and Validator, the KEV listing, Cisco's and Mandiant's indicators, a rating, an ATT&CK mapping and a link to the CVE-2026-20182 entry; both Mandiant sections are corrected in place and workflow references removed. The companion CVE-2026-20127 record gains Cisco's 10.0 score and its KEV listing, and the attacker's file and account names are replaced with descriptions of the behaviour.

Cisco's indicators cover three CLI upload scripts, not only the tenant-list one, and Cisco has seen exploitation push configuration changes to edge devices, which it asks customers to verify; its Live Protect shield is only temporary partial protection. Detection now carries Mandiant's authentication-log, rollback-file and command-history traces, which outlast the actor's cleanup of its root account, in place of the check for UID-0 accounts in /etc/passwd and /etc/shadow, which that cleanup can undo. The action now collects admin-tech before the upgrade and ends with the edge-device configuration check instead of the UID-0 account check.

The weekend of Defused's observation preceded 2026-06-23, not 21 and 22 June; the claim that such scanning historically precedes a targeted wave and the Sysmon and auditd guidance for an appliance had no source; and a test file name served as an indicator. alerts.headline: Exchange OWA flaw used in Russia-aligned espionage is fixed since June 2026, but its mailbox foothold needs removing
alerts.summary: CVE-2026-42897, an exploited cross-site scripting flaw in Outlook Web Access on Exchange 2016, 2019 and Subscription Edition, is fixed in the June 2026 Security Update, and Microsoft recommends the July 2026 update. Proofpoint saw TA488 (Void Blizzard, LAUNDRY BEAR) exploit it from 2026-07-22 with OWAReaper, whose Owner grant to the Default alias on every mail folder survives password resets and re-imaging and needs deliberate removal from the server.

updates.summary: Proofpoint attributed active exploitation of CVE-2026-42897 (the Outlook Web Access stored-XSS flaw Microsoft disclosed on 2026-05-14 and CISA KEV-listed on 2026-05-15) to TA488 (LAUNDRY BEAR / Void Blizzard), the Russian state-supported email-espionage actor that 16 nations jointly exposed on 2026-07-23 over a parallel Zimbra campaign. Merely opening a crafted message in OWA executes "OWAReaper", a JavaScript implant that runs entirely in the reading pane with no host file, harvests browser-autofilled OWA credentials, steals OAuth tokens through mailbox add-ins, and grants the Exchange "Default" alias Owner permission on every mail folder, server-side access that survives credential rotation and device re-imaging. Affected: on-premises Exchange Server 2016/2019/SE at any update level; Exchange Online is not in scope. The permanent fix is the July 2026 Exchange Security Update, and installing it does not remove the earlier mitigation artifacts.

A first source-reliability rating, plus a serialization repair. The first action string was written as a double-quoted YAML scalar containing both a Windows-style path and escaped inner quotes, so a standards-compliant YAML parser rejected the whole frontmatter document; this repo's own lenient parser had always read the intended value. Re-quoted single so the backslash and the inner quotes stay literal. The stored value is byte-identical before and after, and no reader-facing text, claim or field value changed. The entry also carried no Admiralty rating, predating the always-classified gate; A1 is recorded, matching its sourcing: Microsoft's own advisory for its own product is A, and Proofpoint's independent analysis of the implant alongside Microsoft's disclosure is two parties who looked, so credibility 1.

The title, summary, immediate action and first action named the wrong mitigation host (the EM service needs officeclient.microsoft.com), attributed the connectivity requirement to a blog note that only added a known issue, gave an undocumented verification cmdlet on the Edge Transport role where the EM service is not installed, and still said no fix existed. The fix first shipped in the June 2026 Security Update; Microsoft recommends the July update. The main analysis is rewritten to the current state with the EM-service mechanics from Microsoft Learn; the July section is corrected in place (June fix, the joint Proofpoint and NSA release instead of an uncited 16-nation advisory, no workflow vocabulary); an evidence quote is re-attributed to MSRC and one no longer on any cited page is removed; the mitigation-era immediate action and action are removed; priority moves from critical to high now that a fix has existed since June. The flaw is described as cross-site scripting, as Microsoft and Proofpoint describe it, not as stored XSS, and the 2026-07-31 takeaway now dates the fix to June. Exchange Online's exemption is cited to Microsoft's May blog, the 2026-07-31 section calls TA488 Russia-aligned as Proofpoint does, and event_date is the May advisory's date. The 2026-08-30 section is restated in plain language without rating codes. The title, headline and summary no longer say the mitigation must be removed by hand or that the foothold outlives patching: Microsoft says the update does not remove the mitigation, and Proofpoint says the mailbox grant needs deliberate removal. The body no longer says the mitigation must be rolled back or that the foothold outlives patching, the Period 1 end date is cited to the May blog, the 2026-07-31 mechanism paragraphs carry their Proofpoint citation, and the sector tags follow Proofpoint's targets.

Microsoft's May guidance says the Exchange Emergency Mitigation Service cannot check for new mitigations on a server running a build older than March 2023, so such a server never received the automatic mitigation. Proofpoint's two credential behaviours, browser-autofill harvesting and OAuth token theft through mailbox add-ins, are now mapped as credentials from web browsers and stolen application access tokens rather than unsecured credentials. The headline is shortened to the length limit without a change of meaning.

alerts.headline: Attackers exploit a macOS Screen Sharing flaw that lets a network attacker in as root without valid credentials, fixed in 26.6.1
alerts.summary: Apple's macOS 26.6.1, Sequoia 15.7.9 and Sonoma 14.8.9 updates of 2026-08-06 fix CVE-2026-65400 in Screen Sharing, where "an attacker on the network may be able to authenticate to Screen Sharing without valid credentials", addressed through improved state management. The flaw is exploited in the wild: NCSC-NL reported active abuse on 2026-08-12 and CISA added it to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-08-18. It lands one week after macOS reverse-engineer fG! described a pre-authentication file-download bug in the same screensharingd daemon, which Calif counts as a separate flaw fixed in the preceding release and Huntress ties to CVE-2026-65400. Patching and disabling Screen Sharing where it is not needed do not depend on settling that.

updates.summary: Update to this pipeline's 2026-08-08 entry, which carried only Apple's advisory line that an attacker on the network might authenticate to Screen Sharing without valid credentials. Three deltas change the urgency. The daemon that answers those connections runs as root, so this is a pre-authentication remote root primitive rather than a login as one user; researchers rebuilt working exploits from the 26.6.1 binary diff in about four hours, and did the same for a second, independent pre-auth bug in the same source file that Apple closed silently on 2026-07-27 with no CVE; and a researcher scan cited by Calif found roughly 40,000 Macs with Screen Sharing reachable from the internet, and Huntress separately counts tens of thousands of potentially vulnerable hosted bare-metal Macs, noting that some of those providers had not yet folded the fix into their base provisioning images. Calif and Huntress give incompatible root causes for CVE-2026-65400 itself and this entry reports both. Patch to macOS 26.6.1, 15.7.9 or 14.8.9; removing allowed accounts or the VNC password does not help.

CVE-2026-65400, the pre-authentication flaw in the macOS Screen Sharing daemon this pipeline covered on 2026-08-08 and again on 2026-08-11 as having no confirmed in-the-wild exploitation, is now confirmed exploited. NCSC-NL revised advisory NCSC-2026-0280 on 2026-08-12 to record that it had been notified of active abuse observed on multiple systems with port 5900 reachable from the internet, and that in all of those cases root access was obtained and a Monero cryptocurrency miner was planted. Nothing about the remediation changes (macOS 26.6.1, Sequoia 15.7.9 and Sonoma 14.8.9) but the exposed population the prior entry counted at roughly 40,000 hosts now has a confirmed outcome attached to it.

The summary still said no exploitation was reported, and the main text that Apple reported none, after NCSC-NL confirmed active abuse on 2026-08-12 and CISA listed the flaw on 2026-08-18. The main analysis also called it a straightforward patch item with no artifact to look for. It now gives the daemon's root context, the disagreement between Huntress and Calif over which flaw fG!'s proof-of-concept exploited, and Huntress's authentication-type and session-user discriminator, and it drops an unsourced mDNS claim and an unsourced link between the confirmed cases and that discriminator. The 2026-08-11 claim that such a session has no benign explanation is narrowed to Huntress's wording. NCSC-NL reports a planted miner and has not said whether the attacks went further, so the 2026-08-16 text no longer rules out data theft or ransomware.

The CVE record scores CVE-2026-65400 9.8 under CVSS 3.1 (no privileges, no user interaction), above NCSC-NL's 7.1 with low privileges required. Apple credits the flaw to Alfredo Pesoli via Bynario Atlas rather than to fG!, who according to Calif never reported his own screensharingd bug to Apple.

actions: Audit every npm publish token your organisation and its maintainers hold and revoke any that can publish without two-factor authentication: that exact token property, not package popularity, is what decides whether the worm spreads from a compromised developer to your packages.

On any developer workstation or build agent that installed a package from the keyv family since 2026-08-04, or tensorlake@0.5.144 since 2026-10-08, treat the AI-assistant, cloud, GitHub, Vault, SSH and Kubernetes credentials present on that host as disclosed and rotate them; the collector sweeps over 300 credential patterns in one pass, so partial rotation leaves the operator a working set. Isolate the host before revoking its GitHub token, because OX Security reports a switch that wipes the machine when the token is revoked; on a host that ran tensorlake@0.5.144, Socket and OX Security also name a token-monitor persistence (a systemd user unit on Linux, a LaunchAgent on macOS, a scheduled task on Windows), which has to be removed before the token is revoked.

Stop treating a valid npm provenance attestation as evidence a package is clean; where release pipelines gate on provenance, change the check to pin on the workflow identity inside the Fulcio certificate and the Rekor log index, which is what Unit 42 says still discriminates.
alerts.headline: A self-propagating npm worm reaches packages totalling 1.3 billion monthly downloads, and its C2 address lives on-chain
alerts.summary: Elastic Security Labs identified CHAINDROP on 2026-08-04, a new wave of the Shai-Hulud npm worm that began with the compromise of the keyv maintainer and has backdoored over 400 npm packages whose combined reach Elastic puts at more than 1.3 billion monthly downloads, keyv alone at over 600 million. Execution comes from a package.json preinstall hook that downloads the Bun runtime to run an obfuscated 711 KB payload, which harvests over 300 credential patterns (AI-assistant tokens, AWS/GCP/Azure/Alibaba credentials, GitHub tokens, Vault tokens, SSH keys and Kubernetes service-account tokens) and self-propagates only when it finds an npm token that both carries package-write permission and can publish without two-factor authentication. Rather than hardcoding a command-and-control domain, CHAINDROP queries an Ethereum smart contract at runtime to resolve where to send the stolen material, so the operator rotates infrastructure without shipping a new payload. On 2026-10-08 a release of the tensorlake npm SDK carried the same payload family with valid build provenance, and Socket and OX Security describe a dead-man switch that wipes the owner's home directory if the stolen GitHub token is revoked before its persistence is removed.

updates.summary: Unit 42's analysis of CHAINDROP, the Shai-Hulud npm worm wave covered here on 2026-08-06, adds two mechanics that break controls defenders currently rely on. An embedded Python helper opens /proc/<pid>/maps and /proc/<pid>/mem on the GitHub Actions Runner.Worker process and searches live memory for OIDC tokens and runner secrets, so scanning files and environment variables at rest does not see it. A second, single-target path trades a runner OIDC token at npm's trusted-publishing endpoint for a real publish credential, injects a typosquatted dependency without touching install scripts, and then signs the result through Fulcio and Rekor, producing provenance Unit 42 is explicit is not forged.

A further package, tensorlake@0.5.144 (the npm SDK of an AI-agent sandbox platform), was published on 2026-10-08 with a Shai-Hulud-family payload through the project's normal GitHub Actions pipeline with valid build provenance; Socket and OX Security describe the dead-man switch that wipes the owner's home directory when the stolen GitHub token is revoked, and both say to remove its persistence before revoking. Socket matches the release to this wave, while OX Security says new keys may point to an independent actor reusing the name.

Elastic reads the commit-message string warning against token revocation as intimidation, and OX Security calls the same string an extortion string while describing a dead man's switch separately, which Elastic does not mention; the containment paragraph now says so. Unit 42's environment check selects a single republishing path in one project and does not gate the worm as a whole, which the earlier wording implied. The locale-gate sentence gains its citation.

Unit 42 found the August sample's installer for OS-level token-monitor persistence decrypted but never invoked, so in that sample the persistence is a latent capability rather than observed behaviour.

alerts.headline: Gitea Docker instances with reverse-proxy login enabled accepted a spoofed login header from anyone, and NCSC-CH rates it exploited
alerts.summary: Gitea's official Docker image hard-coded REVERSE_PROXY_TRUSTED_PROXIES to the trust-all wildcard, so on instances where an administrator enabled reverse-proxy authentication, anyone who can reach the container's HTTP port can send an X-WEBAUTH-USER header and be signed in as any user whose login name is known or guessable, admins included (CVE-2026-20896, CVSS 9.8). NCSC-CH set it to actively exploited on 2026-07-10. Sysdig, whose telemetry the public reporting rests on, says the attempt it saw had not progressed to exploitation, though SecurityWeek reports the same telemetry as exploitation. Fixed in 1.26.3, and Gitea recommends 1.26.4.

updates.summary: Switzerland's NCSC published an advisory on 2026-07-10 raising the exploitation status of the Gitea Docker-image reverse-proxy auth bypass (CVE-2026-20896, CVSS 9.8) to "Actively Exploited, Proof of Concept Available". The underlying flaw (the official Docker image trusting a spoofable X-WEBAUTH-USER header from any source IP for unauthenticated admin impersonation) was covered on 2026-06-23; the in-window delta is the national-CERT exploitation-status escalation. Public telemetry to date (Sysdig, via SecurityWeek/The Hacker News) still shows only reconnaissance-stage probing, so treat NCSC-CH's "actively exploited" label as a national-authority assessment and prioritise patching internet-reachable Docker instances now.

The main text still said no in-the-wild exploitation was reported after the 2026-07-10 update recorded NCSC-CH's actively-exploited status, and the summary and main text presented the takeover as open to anyone reaching the port. It requires reverse-proxy authentication to be enabled on the official Docker image with the trusted-proxies setting left at the image default, and a known or guessable username. The count of fixed flaws and the description of CVE-2026-27775 are corrected, an unsourced claim that Gitea dominates DACH and EU public-sector DevOps is removed, and hunting advice that relied on a log field no source documents is dropped.

The analysis gains a Triage line from the GitHub advisory: legitimate reverse-proxy logins also carry the X-WEBAUTH-USER header, set by the authenticating proxy, while the exploit sends it on a direct connection from any other source and signs in with no password and no cookie.

alerts.summary: Cisco disclosed CVE-2026-76460 (CVSS 10.0) on 2026-09-16: an unauthenticated, remote authentication bypass in a Cisco Identity Services Engine (ISE) and ISE-PIC API endpoint, affecting ISE and ISE-PIC releases before the fixed patch levels whatever the configuration, that Cisco found during the resolution of a Cisco TAC support case and confirms is under active exploitation. A same-day sibling, CVE-2026-76423 (also CVSS 10.0, not yet confirmed exploited), removes the same authentication boundary via a separate endpoint. There is no workaround; only infrastructure ACLs mitigate.

updates.summary: CVE-2026-76460 was one part of a larger Cisco ISE hardening release the same day: two more CVEs (CVE-2026-20130, CVE-2026-20192) also carry CVSS 10.0, and NCSC-NL scopes the release to 21 vulnerabilities, 13 of them critical. CERT-FR confirms only CVE-2026-76460 is reported exploited, and notes ISE 3.1/3.2 will receive no fix at all for eight of the disclosed CVEs before their November 2027 end of maintenance.

The 2026-09-18 text said no other CVE in the release was named exploited by any source and credited CERT-FR with saying only CVE-2026-76460 is exploited. CERT-FR reports Cisco's statement that CVE-2026-76460 is exploited, Cisco's hardening advisory notes an exploited vulnerability in the class covered by CVE-2026-20192 and points to the CVE-2026-76460 advisory, and Cisco's other advisories report no malicious use. The same text said ISE 3.1 and 3.2 will not receive a fix at all for eight CVEs, where CERT-FR reports only that those trains have not received one, and the eight are now named. A US federal remediation deadline and an uncited claim that ISE is standard infrastructure across enterprise and public-sector networks are removed, and Cisco's advice to re-image nodes where malicious activity is suspected is added.

Cisco says only that the flaw was found during the resolution of a Cisco TAC support case; whose case it was and the contrast with internal research were inference and are removed from title, headline, summary and body. The CWE-grouping clause gains its hardening-advisory citation, CVE-2026-20130 is no longer typed as remote code execution (Cisco describes a grouped output-neutralization class), and the unsupported privilege-escalation technique is dropped.

CVE-2026-76460 and CVE-2026-76423 affect ISE and ISE-PIC releases before the fixed patch levels whatever the configuration, not every release. The access-log check now describes Cisco's search for suspicious usernames without its literal example username.

alerts.summary: CVE-2026-0257 is a pre-auth VPN authentication bypass in PAN-OS GlobalProtect (CISA KEV; Palo Alto reports limited exploit attempts, and Rapid7 and Unit 42 report successful exploitation): an attacker forges valid auth-override cookies by re-using the GlobalProtect certificate shared with the HTTPS service, with no credentials. CISA's KEV catalog (version 2026.10.04) marks it as used in known ransomware campaigns, and Arctic Wolf's report of 2026-07-20 describes June 2026 intrusions in which Qilin ransomware deployment began with this bypass. Unit 42 now names Qilin and Inc as exploiting it and describes one intrusion that pivoted from the VPN gateway to vCenter and ESXi and stole domain credentials offline from a domain controller's virtual disk, which in-guest EDR does not see. Patch or disable auth-override cookies, and treat a gateway that was exposed and unpatched as a compromise-assessment target that includes the virtualization and backup tier.

updates.summary: UPDATE (originally covered 2026-05-30): Unit 42's 9 June update on CVE-2026-0257 confirms that a limited number of probed PAN-OS GlobalProtect devices had attacker-established, gateway-connected VPN sessions, moving this from "exploit attempts observed" to confirmed successful exploitation (Unit 42, 2026-06-09).

PAN-OS GlobalProtect CVE-2026-0257 exploitation wave hits European targets, Arctic Wolf documents Impacket-style SMB lateral movement post-auth-bypass; NCSC-CH refreshed its advisory on 2026-06-16 (§ 4).

CISA's KEV catalog (version 2026.10.04) now marks CVE-2026-0257 as used in known ransomware campaigns, and Arctic Wolf's report of 2026-07-20 describes June 2026 intrusions in which Qilin ransomware deployment began with the bypass, so an exposed, unpatched gateway needs a compromise assessment of the network behind it as well as the patch.

Arctic Wolf's June report describes Impacket-consistent SMB reconnaissance in a subset of intrusions that did not progress beyond session setup, not lateral movement, and its sector list describes the exploitation wave as a whole. Two hunting lines named log fields and Windows event ids no source gives and are rewritten. Unit 42's update of 2026-10-19 and 2026-10-20 names Qilin and Inc as ransomware operators exploiting CVE-2026-0257 and describes one intrusion that pivoted from the VPN gateway to vCenter and ESXi with offline credential theft from a domain controller's virtual disk, so the compromise assessment has to include the virtualization and backup tier.

Palo Alto's advisory makes the one-time re-authentication an automatic consequence of the PAN-OS upgrade, because the fixed firewall regenerates the override cookie, not a step to force; the action and the 2026-06-10 and 2026-10-06 sections now say so.
