immediate_action.title: Patch Ivanti Connect Secure now, then check the appliance and its AD account for compromise

alerts.summary: Ivanti disclosed CVE-2026-104935 on 2026-10-13, an authentication bypass in Connect Secure that lets a remote unauthenticated attacker run commands, and says it is aware of limited exploitation; CISA listed it in KEV the same day. Volexity found a cluster it calls UTA0576 chaining it with a root escalation that Ivanti had not fixed when Volexity reported (a separate record, CVE-2026-111357, now covers that step), patching library code in memory only so Ivanti's Integrity Checker Tool sees no file change, and going after the appliance's Active Directory service account, LAPS passwords and BitLocker recovery keys. Fixed builds are 25.1.1.2, 25.1.3.1 and 22.8R2.5 (Ivanti's own description of the flaw and Rapid7 place 25.1.3.0 outside the affected range, while CERT-FR counts it as affected); a patched appliance that was exposed still needs a compromise check, and CERT-FR says it knows of lateral movement using the LDAP and Active Directory secrets stored on the appliance and tells owners to isolate and preserve it before any reset.

updates.summary: CERT-FR's alert of 2026-10-14 says it knows of lateral movement using the LDAP and Active Directory secrets stored on the appliance, and sets the response order: isolate the appliance from the internet and the internal network, snapshot and keep it powered on, then analyse before any reset; its rotation scope also covers Kerberos tickets of the service accounts and licence-server authentication. CERT-FR also counts 25.1.3.0 as affected, so the fixed-build targets now name 25.1.3.1.

The unfixed root-escalation step of the chain now has its own identifier, CVE-2026-111357, published 2026-10-15, and the Canadian Cyber Centre says open-source reporting indicates it is exploited in the wild; its description names only 22.8R2.4 as affected, says the step was exploited in the wild in October 2026 and states no fixed build, so scanners, SIEM enrichment and tickets can now follow the step by ID.

The status of build 25.1.3.0 now rests on Ivanti's own description of the flaw, which covers versions before 25.1.3.0, beside Rapid7's table and CERT-FR's alert, which counts 25.1.3.0 as affected; 25.1.3.1 stays the target build.

actions: Confirm every Kemp LoadMaster runs GA 7.2.63.2 or LTSF 7.2.54.18 or later, and disable the LoadMaster API wherever it is not required, which removes the /accessv2 attack surface.

For any LoadMaster that was internet-reachable with the API enabled before it was patched, run a compromise assessment of the appliance rather than closing the ticket on the version string: a public exploit has circulated since 2026-06-29.

cves.affected: LoadMaster GA 7.2.60.0 to 7.2.63.1 and LTSF 7.2.54.12 to 7.2.54.17, when the API is enabled; ECS Connections Manager, Object Scale Connection Manager and MOVEit WAF 7.2.60.0 to 7.2.63.1

alerts.headline: Progress Kemp LoadMaster pre-auth RCE in the /accessv2 API is exploited in the wild and KEV-listed, with fixes in GA 7.2.63.2 and LTSF 7.2.54.18
alerts.summary: Progress Kemp LoadMaster pre-auth RCE (CVE-2026-8037, CVSS 9.6 per Progress, 9.8 per ZDI): uninitialized-malloc heap corruption in the /accessv2 API reaches code execution as root. watchTowr published the full mechanics, exploitation attempts began on 2026-06-29 and CISA added the flaw to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-08-07; the fix is in GA v7.2.63.2 and LTSF v7.2.54.18.

updates.summary: Kemp LoadMaster exploitation now confirmed. eSentire reports in-the-wild exploitation attempts against the pre-auth command-injection CVE-2026-8037 began 29 June (the same day a public PoC dropped) though observed attempts failed (eSentire TRU).

CISA added CVE-2026-8037 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-08-07, based on evidence of active exploitation of the unauthenticated command-injection flaw in Progress Kemp LoadMaster. When this pipeline last covered it on 2026-07-02 the only observed activity was exploitation attempts that eSentire reported as unsuccessful. Every LoadMaster running a version at or below GA 7.2.63.1, or the LTSF release 7.2.54.17, with the API enabled is affected; any appliance that sat internet-reachable and unpatched between the 29 June proof-of-concept and now warrants a compromise assessment rather than an upgrade alone.

After the 2026-07-02 and 2026-08-08 updates recorded exploitation attempts from 2026-06-29 and CISA's KEV listing of 2026-08-07, the summary and main text still said Progress reported no known exploitation, which was Progress's position at disclosure on 2026-06-04. The headline and summary now state the current exploitation status, and the main text dates Progress's no-exploitation statement to disclosure. The description of the second bulletin CVE, CVE-2026-33691, no longer names OWASP CRS. The LTSF fixed build 7.2.54.18 is named, the 9.8 score is attributed to ZDI next to eSentire's 9.6, and the patch and compromise-assessment steps no longer overlap.

eSentire's assessment is that exploitation attempts will increase, after every attempt it observed failed; it did not forecast more successful attacks. The catalog description, CWE and ransomware flag are cited to CISA's catalog record rather than its alert, which carries none of them. The main analysis gains its Exposure, Detection and Defender takeaway lines, and the detection paragraph keeps only what watchTowr shows as sourced.

Progress, the numbering authority, scores CVE-2026-8037 at 9.6 for an adjacent-network attacker, the score eSentire reports, while 9.8 is ZDI's; the CVE record bounds the affected LoadMaster builds at GA 7.2.60.0 to 7.2.63.1 and LTSF 7.2.54.12 to 7.2.54.17 and also lists ECS Connections Manager, Object Scale Connection Manager and MOVEit WAF, now named as affected. CVE-2026-33691 is an OWASP Core Rule Set flaw, as Progress's release notes say, so the attribution an earlier correction removed is restored, with its 6.8 CVE score. The main text gains a Triage line from watchTowr's request, and the hunting notes are marked as inference.

actions: Upgrade TeamCity On-Premises to 2025.11.7 or 2026.1.3 on the matching branch, or install JetBrains' security-patch plugin where the version is older than that but at least 2017.1, and until that is done restrict external access to the TeamCity server, as JetBrains advises, because the flaw needs nothing but HTTP(S) reachability.

Treat any TeamCity On-Premises server that was internet-reachable and still unpatched at any point after 2026-07-27 as a compromise-assessment target rather than a completed patch: review build-agent registrations for agents you did not enrol, and rotate the VCS credentials, artifact-repository tokens and signing keys the server holds, because an upgrade evicts the entry point but not what was taken through it.

cves.affected: All TeamCity On-Premises versions prior to the branch fixes; TeamCity Cloud already mitigated by JetBrains.
cves.fixed: 2025.11.7 and 2026.1.3, with JetBrains' security-patch plugin as the mitigation path for installations from 2017.1 onward that cannot take the full upgrade.

alerts.headline: JetBrains patches an unauthenticated remote-code-execution flaw reachable on every TeamCity On-Premises version ever shipped
alerts.summary: JetBrains disclosed CVE-2026-63077 on 2026-07-27: an attacker with nothing more than HTTP(S) access to a TeamCity On-Premises server can exploit the agent-polling protocol to bypass authentication checks and execute arbitrary operating-system commands as the TeamCity server process. Every On-Premises version is affected; fixes are 2025.11.7 and 2026.1.3, with a security-patch plugin available down to 2017.1 for estates that cannot upgrade immediately, and JetBrains says TeamCity Cloud needs no customer action because it is already mitigated. CISA listed the flaw as exploited on 2026-08-05, JetBrains reported active and attempted exploitation of unpatched servers on 2026-08-07, CISA's KEV catalog now marks known ransomware campaign use, and JetBrains' own Cadence service was breached through it. A build server compromise is a supply-chain compromise.

updates.summary: CISA added CVE-2026-63077 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-08-05 based on evidence of active exploitation, changing the status of the unauthenticated JetBrains TeamCity On-Premises remote-code- execution flaw covered here on 2026-07-29 from patch-available to confirmed exploited. JetBrains' advisory, unchanged since 2026-07-27, still records that it was not aware of any active exploitation at publication. No authority has named an exploiting cluster or the observed intrusion path. Because every On-Premises version ever shipped is affected and the flaw needs only HTTP(S) reachability, any TeamCity server that was internet-reachable and unpatched before 2026-08-05 now warrants a compromise assessment rather than only an upgrade.

CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog now marks CVE-2026-63077 as used in ransomware campaigns. Ransomware operators are now exploiting the unauthenticated TeamCity On-Premises RCE, so any server that was reachable and unpatched needs the compromise assessment, not only the upgrade. The summary and main text no longer say exploitation is unobserved. CWE-502 now cites CISA's KEV record, and a numeric score that no citable source publishes is removed. JetBrains' 2026-08-07 confirmation of active exploitation and its log indicators lead the detection and triage lines, an Exposure line gives the fixed versions, TeamCity Cloud is described as already mitigated rather than unaffected, the sourcing note describes only cited sources, and two citation dates follow the pages.

The verification value moves to multi-source (JetBrains' exploitation follow-up and CISA's catalog listing are independent statements), and two sentences are reworded so they describe what JetBrains published rather than claim it withheld a gadget chain, and do not refer to the entry itself. The main analysis gains the current Defender takeaway (patch, then treat exposed unpatched servers as incident cases because of the recorded ransomware use), and the sentence on what a server holds now follows JetBrains' own wording. The sourcing note no longer says JetBrains withholds details.

JetBrains, as numbering authority, scores CVE-2026-63077 CVSS 3.1 9.8 in the CVE record, although its blog advisory gives no number. Because JetBrains reports exploitation since its 2026-07-27 announcement, the compromise-assessment window now starts on that date, and the interim mitigation follows JetBrains: restrict external access to the whole server rather than to one endpoint.

On TeamCity 2024.03 and newer the security patch plugin for CVE-2026-63077 is downloaded automatically but still has to be applied from Administration | Updates, under Available security updates; until a fix is in place, JetBrains strongly recommends temporarily restricting external access to internet-facing servers.

alerts.headline: node-ipc npm package backdoored, likely via an expired-domain maintainer takeover: three malicious versions steal developer and CI credentials on require()
alerts.summary: node-ipc npm package (widely-used Node.js IPC library) hijacked, likely via an expired-domain account takeover; three malicious versions (9.1.6, 9.2.3, 12.0.1) exfiltrate cloud, CI/CD, SSH and Keychain credentials over DNS TXT (StepSecurity also reports an HTTPS channel that Socket did not find); rotate every secret on any workstation or CI runner that loaded one of the three versions (Socket Security, 2026-05-14 · StepSecurity, 2026-05-14).

updates.summary: Unsourced claims are removed: a named registrar, Vue CLI and webpack dependents, registry removal of the versions and an npm audit bypass, along with advice to run npm ci with scripts disabled, which does not stop a payload that fires on require(). The conflicting payload descriptions of Socket and StepSecurity are stated as a contradiction, so the title no longer asserts StepSecurity's pattern count. An attacker-controlled domain, the exfiltration DNS suffix, the maintainer email domain and account name and inline ATT&CK ids are removed, the truncated headline is rewritten, and the entry gains an ATT&CK mapping.

The expired-domain takeover is Socket's likely vector, not an established one, and StepSecurity offers a different explanation; the title, headline and summary now say likely. CSO Online's article is dated 2026-05-15, not 2026-05-14.

As of 2026-10-21 the npm registry no longer lists the malicious 9.1.6, 9.2.3 and 12.0.1 releases and its latest tag points to 14.0.0, so a fresh unpinned install no longer resolves to one of them; the exposure now lies with hosts and caches that already hold one of the three.

actions: Audit every internet-facing FortiGate for administrator accounts and REST API keys nobody created, then terminate all administrator and VPN sessions and reset every administrator and VPN password.
alerts.headline: FBI and Secret Service: FortiBleed is still active, locks admins out of FortiGates and feeds ransomware affiliates
alerts.summary: FortiBleed is an active credential-compromise campaign against internet-facing FortiGate firewalls and SSL VPN gateways, with SOCRadar counting more than 86,644 compromised devices in 194 countries; Fortinet said in June that it uses no new vulnerability, only reused credentials and brute force. A joint FBI and U.S. Secret Service advisory of 2026-10-06 says attackers keep scanning exposed devices with previously obtained credentials, create administrator accounts on compromised firewalls and in some cases delete or change the original accounts so owners are locked out, and that access brokers using the chain have supplied INC/Lynx and Payload ransomware affiliates. An organisation with an internet-exposed FortiGate should end all administrator and VPN sessions, reset every credential and look for accounts and API keys it did not create.

updates.summary: FortiBleed escalates to 86,644 compromised FortiGate devices; CISA issues emergency hardening guidance. Up from 73,932 (covered 2026-06-18); attackers are cracking SSL VPN password hashes and pivoting into Active Directory (§ 4).

The FortiBleed credential-harvesting campaign got its first full tool-chain disclosure: a Golang "FortigateSniffer" that abuses FortiOS's native diagnose sniffer packet to capture auth traffic, a PCAP converter, and a 36-GPU offline-cracking cluster, with Fortinet confirming no new CVE, only credential reuse and brute force. The detection opportunity is the sniffer's own footprint (BleepingComputer, 2026-06-22).

A joint FBI and U.S. Secret Service advisory of 2026-10-06 says FortiBleed is still active: the operators create administrator accounts on compromised FortiGates and in some cases delete or change the original accounts, locking owners out, and access brokers using the chain have supplied INC/Lynx and Payload ransomware affiliates. It cites SOCRadar for more than 86,644 compromised devices and adds firewall, VPN and domain controller log review, REST API key review and PBKDF2 enforcement to the response.

The June hunting paragraph named Windows event ids and a domain-wide rotation that no cited source gives; Fortinet's guidance is to treat directory accounts the device used as compromised and review domain controller logs. The October paragraph had attributed a FortiGate audit-log mapping to the FBI and Secret Service advisory, which names only the logs to review. The action keeps the single do-now task.

The June dataset figures come from three researchers, and BleepingComputer reports firewall URLs and apparently valid credentials, some confirmed authentic, rather than management URLs and valid credentials: Hudson Rock counted 73,932 URLs in 194 countries and 21,632 domains, Kevin Beaumont put it at about 75,000 devices. SOCRadar's Lynx / INC attribution dates from its 29 June update, while BleepingComputer's October recap dates it to July. The Detection line adds the FBI and Secret Service configuration review, with particular attention to added unrecognized accounts, and the account deletions and password changes they report on compromised devices.

actions: **Patch the LiteSpeed cPanel plugin (CVE-2026-54420)** by upgrading to LiteSpeed WHM PlugIn version 5.3.2.1, which bundles cPanel plugin 2.4.8, or uninstall the user-end plugin until then. It is actively exploited on shared CloudLinux/CageFS hosting. Prioritise any public-sector tenant on shared hosting.

cves.affected: LiteSpeed user-end cPanel plugin before 2.4.8

alerts.headline: CVE-2026-54420: LiteSpeed cPanel plugin root escalation on CloudLinux/CageFS shared hosting, exploited in the wild (CISA KEV)
alerts.summary: LiteSpeed user-end cPanel plugin CVE-2026-54420 lets a user with FTP or web-shell access escalate to root on CloudLinux/CageFS shared hosting and is actively exploited; its CVE record dates the in-the-wild exploitation to May 2026, and LiteSpeed was alerted on 2026-05-31 (LiteSpeed, 2026-06-01). Added to CISA KEV on 2026-06-15 (CISA, 2026-06-15). Patch to WHM PlugIn 5.3.2.1 (cPanel plugin 2.4.8).

updates.summary: The text said the flaw enables cross-account file access and cited NVD for exploitation and an 8.5 score. LiteSpeed, the vendor, describes escalation to root and active exploitation, and says only its user-end cPanel plugin, not its WHM plugin, is affected. The text, title, headline, summary and action now state what LiteSpeed publishes without an exploitation start in May, the 8.5 score is re-cited to The Hacker News, and a detection line gives LiteSpeed's own log check. An exposure line follows LiteSpeed's wording, the main text gains a cited takeaway, and the affected LiteSpeed cPanel Plugin is named.

The CVE record dates the in-the-wild exploitation of CVE-2026-54420 to May 2026, with LiteSpeed's 2026-05-31 as only the date it was alerted, so the entry no longer drops the May dating and the log check now covers servers upgraded since. The CVE record's affected and fixed versions are filled in, the vector reflects a no-interaction attack by a user with FTP or web-shell access, the CVE description's boundary (WHM PlugIn before version 5.3.2.0) is noted beside LiteSpeed's fixed version 5.3.2.1, and LiteSpeed's false-positive discriminators become a Triage line.

actions: Upgrade every self-hosted JFrog Artifactory instance to a build that closes both CVEs: 7.133.11 or later for CVE-2026-42016, which JFrog names as its only fixed build, and the CVE-2026-42018 fix for the branch, where Wiz's corrected builds (7.133.29, 7.146.38, 7.161.20) sit above JFrog's table. Wiz's 7.111.21, 7.117.28 and 7.125.20 are below 7.133.11, so instances on those branches remain vulnerable to CVE-2026-42016 and must move to 7.133.11 or later.

On any Artifactory instance that was internet-reachable and unpatched since 15 August 2026, search access logs for an unauthenticated POST to /access/api/v1/aws/token/ followed by a POST to /access/api/v1/tokens from the same client (in some cases Wiz saw an admin account created within five minutes of the first request); on a hit with both answered HTTP 200, treat the instance as compromised and reset the Access token signing key and certificate before relying on the upgrade.

cves.affected: JFrog Artifactory (Self-Hosted) before 7.133.11

alerts.headline: Two JFrog Artifactory bugs patched weeks ago are confirmed chained into full admin takeover

immediate_action.action: Wiz Research confirms active, ongoing exploitation of this two-CVE chain against self-hosted JFrog Artifactory since 15 August 2026, reaching full administrative control and, in multiple cases, a dropped Rust-based backdoor with C2 capability. Six weeks after disclosure, most organizations running Artifactory still have at least one vulnerable instance. Upgrade every instance to 7.133.11 or later, JFrog's only fixed build for CVE-2026-42016, on a build that also carries the CVE-2026-42018 fix for its branch. Wiz lists 7.133.29, 7.146.38 and 7.161.20 for those branches, above JFrog's own table. Wiz's lower-branch builds 7.111.21, 7.117.28 and 7.125.20 stay inside JFrog's affected range for CVE-2026-42016. Then search access logs for the chain's own signature: an unauthenticated POST to /access/api/v1/aws/token/ followed by a POST to /access/api/v1/tokens from the same client (in some cases Wiz saw an admin account created within five minutes of the first request). A hit where both requests returned HTTP 200 is a successful exploitation: treat the instance as compromised. Revoke all tokens, reset the Access token signing key and certificate, audit for administrator accounts you did not create, remove unauthorized Groovy plugins and restart the JVM to clear any in-memory implant.
immediate_action.title: Patch and hunt JFrog Artifactory now: confirmed admin-takeover chain, backdoors already dropped

alerts.summary: Wiz Research documents in-the-wild exploitation, running 15 August–8 September 2026, of two distinct JFrog Artifactory flaws, CVE-2026-42018 (an unauthenticated caller can obtain an internal anonymous-user token) and CVE-2026-42016 (that token's scope is not validated when exchanged for a new one), chained into an unauthenticated-to-admin escalation in two HTTP requests, in some cases reaching a created administrator account in under five minutes. Both CVEs were disclosed and patched by JFrog in July and August, weeks before this exploitation was reported; six weeks after disclosure, 59% of organizations running Artifactory remained vulnerable to CVE-2026-42016, and CVE-2026-42018 fell only from 69% to 62% over four weeks.

updates.summary: The 8.1 and 7.5 scores came from the MITRE CVE records, and the cited advisory pages do not carry them. They are removed from the text and the structured data, and the severity sentence now cites JFrog's advisory page, which rates both flaws High. The fixed-build guidance now requires 7.133.11 or later for CVE-2026-42016, which JFrog names as its only fixed build, and states the conflict between JFrog's CVE-2026-42018 table and Wiz's corrected, higher builds. The scope-escalation consequence is attributed to Wiz, the compromise check adds Wiz's signing-key reset and in-memory implant caveat, the triage line names the bare token path correctly, the kill-chain, post-exploitation and patch-velocity paragraphs now cite Wiz, and the sourcing note keeps provenance only. The log-search guidance now counts a hit as successful exploitation only when both requests returned HTTP 200, and the takeaway no longer says one fix leaves the chain intact.
A Wiz Research quotation was not verbatim (an ellipsis replaced part of the sentence); it now quotes Wiz's sentence as written. The compromise-check action is trimmed to the task itself.

JFrog's own CVSS 3.1 scores from its CVE records, 8.1 for CVE-2026-42016 and 7.5 for CVE-2026-42018, are restored with ENISA's EU Vulnerability Database as the citation; the advisory page itself shows only the High label. The log-search guidance no longer says the two token requests come within minutes of each other, since Wiz gives only an under-five-minutes time to a created admin account in some cases. The headline drops "dormant", BSI's advisory is described as recording an exploit rather than KEV status, and EPSS is refreshed to FIRST's 2026-10-20 scores.

actions: Take every self-hosted Langflow instance off any internet-reachable interface: ZDI documents no fixed version and names restricting interaction with the product as the only mitigation, so network position is the whole of the available control.

On any Langflow host that was internet-exposed, rotate the LLM-provider API keys and any other service credentials that instance held or could read: VulnCheck reports credential harvesting as observed post-exploitation behaviour, and those keys are billable and usable from anywhere.

cves.affected: 1.3.2, the only version ZDI's CVE record lists; no affected range is defined and ZDI's advisory names none
cves.fixed: None documented; ZDI's mitigation is to restrict interaction with the product

alerts.headline: VulnCheck's canaries show attackers exploiting a Langflow pre-auth RCE with no documented fix and no KEV entry, while the next CVE number is KEV-listed
alerts.summary: VulnCheck reported on 2026-07-28 that it has observed attackers gaining initial access to Langflow with exploits targeting CVE-2026-0769 and a second Langflow flaw, CVE-2026-5027, then harvesting credentials, deploying cryptominers and attempting lateral movement, without splitting that activity between the two, and that neither flaw is in CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog. CVE-2026-0769 is a Zero Day Initiative 0-day advisory: an eval injection in Langflow's eval_custom_component_code function reachable with no authentication (CVSS 9.8), for which ZDI documents no fixed version and names restricting interaction with the product as the only mitigation. A KEV-driven patch process will not surface this, and the KEV-listed CVE-2026-0770, the next CVE number, is a different vulnerability.

updates.summary: The earlier text described the CVE record's contents, including a single tested version 1.3.2 and CISA's enrichment status, from a source that is not a published advisory. ZDI's own advisory gives the 9.8 score and names no affected or fixed version. The earlier count of five Langflow CVEs in KEV is updated to the six listed in the 2026-09-29 catalog, which still omits CVE-2026-0769, and unsupported statements that OSV has no record and that CVE-2026-0770 has a patch path are removed. CVE-2026-0769 and CVE-2026-0770 are consecutive numbers, not one digit apart. The title, headline and text now say no fix is documented rather than that none exists.

VulnCheck's observed intrusions used exploits for both CVE-2026-0769 and CVE-2026-5027, and it does not split the credential harvesting, cryptominers and lateral movement between them. ZDI's CVE record lists Langflow 1.3.2 as the only affected version while its advisory names none, so the affected range is undefined rather than unpublished.

actions: Update Ninja Forms to 3.15.4 or later and WPC Product Bundles for WooCommerce to 8.6.7 or later on every WordPress site, then check each site for an implant the update does not remove, starting with a comparison of the database's administrator list against the Users screen and an inspection of the must-use plugins directory by content.

On any site where an administrator opened a Ninja Forms submission or a WooCommerce order since 2026-10-04 and an implant turns up, rotate all privileged credentials and the WordPress authentication salts and treat the oldest administrator account as compromised, because a login URL planted by the implant authenticates as that account.

cves.affected: Ninja Forms up to and including 3.15.3
WPC Product Bundles for WooCommerce up to and including 8.6.6
Ninja Forms up to and including 3.15.3 (the same flaw as CVE-2026-94504, published by another CVE Numbering Authority)

alerts.headline: Exploited WordPress plugin XSS ends in a hidden admin and persistence that patching does not remove
alerts.summary: Patchstack reports that since 2026-10-04 one campaign has been exploiting two unrelated stored cross-site scripting flaws, CVE-2026-93836 in WPC Product Bundles for WooCommerce up to 8.6.6 and CVE-2026-94504 in Ninja Forms up to 3.15.3, by planting a script in an order or a form submission that runs when a logged-in administrator opens it. The script uses the administrator's own session to install a malicious plugin and create administrators, one of them hidden from the Users screen, and leaves four independent ways back in, so updating to Ninja Forms 3.15.4 or WPC Product Bundles 8.6.7 stops new injections but does not evict an implant. Patchstack says exploitation volume is limited so far and that the second stage works with any stored XSS that reaches an administrator.

updates.summary: Adds CVE-2026-92438, the id under which another CVE Numbering Authority published the same Ninja Forms flaw as CVE-2026-94504, so that advisories and scanners keyed on either id match; updating to 3.15.4 resolves both.

actions: **Patch Check Point IKEv1 VPN gateways now (CVE-2026-50751)**: apply hotfix sk185033, disable deprecated IKEv1 remote-access support or enforce machine-certificate authentication, and review gateway logs from 7 May 2026 for completed IKEv1 Quick Mode ("Key Install") events before the fix that come from unrecognised users or source IP addresses.

alerts.headline: Check Point IKEv1 VPN auth bypass exploited since 7 May, actor assessed with medium confidence to use Qilin. CISA KEV, public PoC, apply sk185033

immediate_action.action: An unauthenticated attacker can forge a Remote Access / Mobile Access VPN session without a valid password on gateways running the deprecated IKEv1 key exchange, and the flaw has been exploited in the wild since 7 May 2026, a month before disclosure, against a few dozen targeted organizations. Check Point confirmed Qilin-affiliate post-compromise activity in one case and assesses with medium confidence that the exploiting actor uses Qilin ransomware. NCSC-CH has issued an advisory flagging the CVE as actively exploited. Apply hotfix sk185033 now, disable legacy IKEv1 remote-access client support, and review gateway logs from 7 May for completed IKEv1 Quick Mode ("Key Install") events before the fix that come from unrecognised users or source IP addresses, as Check Point's sk185033 advises.
immediate_action.title: Patch Check Point IKEv1 VPN gateways (CVE-2026-50751)

alerts.summary: Check Point IKEv1 VPN auth bypass (CVE-2026-50751, CVSS 9.3) exploited in the wild since 7 May, a month before disclosure, against a few dozen targeted organizations. Check Point confirmed post-compromise activity associated with a Qilin ransomware affiliate in one case and assesses with medium confidence that the actor behind the exploitation is financially motivated and uses Qilin ransomware (Check Point, 2026-06-08). Unauthenticated session forgery on Remote Access / Mobile Access gateways. NCSC-CH flagged it as actively exploited (NCSC-CH, 2026-06-08) and CISA added it to KEV (CISA KEV catalog, 2026-06-08).

updates.summary: UPDATE (originally covered 2026-06-09): NCSC-NL updated its advisory (NCSC-2026-0179, version 1.0.1) on 2026-06-16 to note that public proof-of-concept code is now available for the Check Point Security Gateway IKEv1 authentication bypass (CVE-2026-50751, CVSS 9.3), increasing the probability of exploitation …

The CVE statuses were swapped: CVE-2026-50751 (the exploited, KEV-listed flaw) lacked the exploited and KEV markers while the unexploited companion CVE-2026-50752 carried them. The statuses now match the sources, the broken pointer to a brief section is replaced by a link to the companion deep-dive entry, and two overlapping actions are merged. The headline, title, summary and immediate action now give Check Point's one confirmed Qilin-affiliate case and its medium-confidence actor assessment separately, the NCSC-CH advisory is no longer called Action-Required, and CVE-2026-50752 is typed as a certificate-validation logic flaw enabling a site-to-site MitM under specific conditions. alerts.headline: Metabase Cloud was breached through its own 0-day; self-hosted instances stay vulnerable until manually upgraded

Cloud instances were patched by the vendor; self-hosted deployments stay vulnerable until manually upgraded to 0.58.24, 0.59.21, 0.60.17, 0.61.11, 0.62.9 or 0.63.5. Laptop maker Framework and form builder Tally were the first to confirm customer data was taken, on 2026-08-03. The flaw went a week without a CVE identifier before it was assigned CVE-2026-72898 and added to CISA's KEV catalog on 2026-08-11. updates.summary: Metabase's unauthenticated SQL-injection zero-day, covered here on 2026-08-09 when no CVE existed, has been assigned CVE-2026-72898 in GitHub Security Advisory GHSA-vwf4-m7j8-wcjf at CVSS 3.1 10.0, and CISA added it to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-08-11. The advisory publishes affected ranges per release line and confirms active exploitation in Metabase's own words. For self-hosted instances nothing about the exposure changed, but the flaw is now visible to every scanner, SBOM pipeline and CVE-keyed patch process that could not see it a week ago.

A tracker maintained by VenariX, updated 2026-08-17, now counts nine publicly confirmed organisations whose compromised Metabase environments were used to reach connected data warehouses, n8n, Framework, Tally and Kilo Code, joined on 2026-08-17 by Stocksy United Co-op, ShipMonk, Checkly, Cypress.io and Bits of Gold. This pipeline covered CVE-2026-72898 on 2026-08-09 and 2026-08-12 as an exploited CVSS 10.0 unauthenticated SQL injection in the password-reset endpoint; the delta is the downstream pattern. Because Metabase stores the credentials for every database it connects to, administrative access to the application yields those credentials, and Metabase's own guidance is that patching does not invalidate credentials already exposed. Metabase also published a two-request log pattern that indicates a given instance was compromised.

The downstream victim list grows again through a further intermediary: Shipup, a French package-tracking platform used by 700+ e-commerce brands, was compromised through the same vulnerability, and at least six of its retail clients, including Carrefour, Printemps, Citadium, Aroma-Zone, Micromania and Easypara, have since notified their own customers of exposed contact data.

The Shipup section claimed the 31 July to 17 August access window was the same one this entry's earlier coverage had already established for the campaign. The sentence now states that difference instead of asserting agreement. Recorded for the audit trail and not otherwise fixable: the changelog record of the same day declared a change to the evidence list that its commit did not make.

VenariX's tracker now counts fifteen publicly confirmed downstream incidents, up from nine, adding Privy, Paradigm Connect Asia, Statista, Dodo Payments, Marsello and LEGO Certified Stores South Africa. It attributes two of them, at Statista and Dodo Payments, to the Dire Wolf ransomware and extortion group exploiting self-hosted Metabase, and suspects fourteen more targets. Dodo Payments' own disclosure confirms a self-hosted Metabase instance breached through CVE-2026-72898. CVE-2026-88771 requires no configuration at all: every default deployment is reachable by an unauthenticated attacker; CVE-2026-88772 is reachable wherever DTLS is enabled, which Citrix states is the default on any VPN virtual server. Citrix lists no workaround, and Mandiant's interim network controls (disable DTLS where it is not needed, block inbound UDP/443 upstream) cover CVE-2026-88772 only. alerts.summary: Citrix's CTX697096 bulletin (2026-09-27) fixes eight NetScaler ADC/Gateway flaws, two of which, CVE-2026-88771 (unauthenticated command execution, every default deployment) and CVE-2026-88772 (memory overflow to RCE/DoS, reachable wherever DTLS is enabled, the VPN-vServer default), were exploited before any fix existed; CISA added both to KEV and Citrix lists no workaround. Mandiant, GTIG, Unit 42, Zscaler and Rapid7 describe the compromises: web-server-configuration persistence, web shells, and in one intrusion the SAML crash CVE-2026-88779 chained with CVE-2026-88771 so that the crash handler ran the payload as root, followed by exfiltration of the appliance configuration and key material. An appliance patched after the bulletin therefore still needs a compromise check and its configuration secrets rotated. SAML-configured appliances need the later builds named for CVE-2026-88779 (14.1-73.41 or 13.1-64.28) and identity providers 14.1-73.46 or 13.1-64.29 for CVE-2026-107406; CVE-2026-88773 has a public proof of concept with no exploitation seen.

updates.summary: watchTowr Labs published a full root-cause analysis on 2026-09-28: the vulnerable component for CVE-2026-88771 is ns_monuploadd_err.pl, a crash-log-monitoring script, not the nsppe packet engine historically named in NetScaler CVEs, and the trigger is not limited to the SSLVPN login form: any endpoint or port that logs attacker-controlled header data can poison the log the script later parses. watchTowr also confirms per-CVE exploitation status across the bulletin (only CVE-2026-88771 and CVE-2026-88772 exploited; the rest patched but not reported exploited, matching this entry's existing table) and published a public detection tool. NCSC-CH, NCSC-UK and CERT-FR each issued same-day advisories confirming active exploitation.

Google's Mandiant and GTIG report the exploitation campaign has run since at least early September, with government among the impacted sectors in North America and Europe, and describe post-exploitation web-server-configuration persistence, the WHIPSHOT web shell and the SLAPSHOT tunneler; eSentire places CVE-2026-88771 exploitation from 5 September. watchTowr published the CVE-2026-88772 root cause and NCSC Switzerland now lists a proof of concept for both flaws. Mandiant's interim controls (disable DTLS, block UDP/443 upstream) cover CVE-2026-88772 only, NetScaler 12.1 and 13.0 are end of life with no fix, and a shared municipal operator in Rhineland-Palatinate shut down citizen-service systems statewide as a precaution, a shutdown heise links to these NetScaler updates while the operators name no vendor.

Palo Alto Networks Unit 42's threat brief adds first-party telemetry: version fingerprinting of NetScaler Gateways from 2026-08-21, web shells delivered as .deb packages from the client-installer folder between 2026-09-04 and 2026-09-24, and a three-stage log-poisoning chain seen on 2026-09-21, with the log artifacts each leaves. Earlier text is corrected: the KEV remediation deadline is dropped; the evidence to capture before patching is an instance snapshot where the appliance is virtual (not a configuration snapshot), cited to watchTowr and Unit 42; the triage discriminator for CVE-2026-88771 now describes the logged crash-message imitation instead of a valid-session premise; the NCSC-CH, NCSC UK and CERT-FR advisories are described as relaying Citrix's confirmation, with links; the pre-notification reported by BleepingComputer is no longer presented as the source of the shutdown calls; a stale statement that NCSC-CH had not yet published an advisory is replaced; and a dead Censys link points to its canonical page.

Citrix's bulletin CTX697174 (2026-10-03) fixes CVE-2026-88779, a SAML-triggered memory overflow that the September fixed builds do not cover; Citrix confirms targeted attacks and tells SAML-configured appliances that already took the September builds to upgrade again, to 14.1-73.41, 13.1-64.28 or the FIPS builds.

The headline says Citrix has published no workaround. The Triage line follows watchTowr's root-cause analysis for CVE-2026-88771 and GTIG's log artifacts for CVE-2026-88772, which GTIG advises alerting on individually, and the zero-day timing is cited to watchTowr. Only Mandiant's DTLS and UDP/443 controls are limited to CVE-2026-88772 and its upstream IP allow-listing is not tied to one flaw, the KEV sentence drops the US directive, a reference to an exploitation table that does not exist is removed, and the takeaway adds GTIG's sector statement.

The pointers to the SAML builds now carry the 2026-10-08 bulletin CTX697191: identity-provider appliances need 14.1-73.46 or 13.1-64.29 (or the FIPS builds) after the 14.1-73.41 and 13.1-64.28 builds, which Citrix lists as affected by CVE-2026-107406.

Rapid7's incident analysis of an early-October NetScaler compromise shows CVE-2026-88771 chained with the SAML crash CVE-2026-88779, with the call-home crash handler running the payload as root after a reboot, followed by persistence that synchronises to the HA peer, internal reconnaissance and exfiltration of the appliance configuration and key material; an appliance that was reached needs the configuration secrets rotated as well as the patch.

actions: Upgrade every PaperCut NG/MF Application Server, Site Server and secondary/print server to the security maintenance release for its line (26.0.5, 25.0.13 or 24.1.11, the v24 build the September bulletin now names), starting with any still on Emergency Patch Release 1 or 2, because the emergency builds do not carry the fix for CVE-2026-82077, an administrator-only Scan-to-Fax code-execution flaw that the vendor's September bulletin lists as fixed in 26.0.5, 25.0.13 and 24.1.10; for v23 and earlier, immediately restrict the Application Server's web interface to trusted/internal IP addresses only; no patch exists for that line. On every server, patched or not, set the advanced config key auth.webservices.auth-token to a long random secret and limit auth.webservices.allowed-addresses to the hosts that call the XML-RPC API, because Hunt.io says an instance hardened against the Tapestry bypass is not necessarily protected against the XML-RPC route it recovered, which works when the allowlist is too permissive or no token is set.

Before patching or restarting an internet-facing server, preserve the server/logs directory and process tree; check server.log for the two vendor-documented error strings and for an unexplained gap or truncation, check server.log and derby.log for an in-memory Derby database booted under an attacker-chosen name, and hunt for a Windows service named "Remote Access Service" running SimpleService.exe (SimpleHelp) or an unexpected AnyDesk install, as PaperCut's own published incident data names both as an observed post-compromise access method.

Given GreyNoise's confirmed domain-admin escalation paths, verify no PaperCut Application Server is domain-joined with a privileged service account or hosted on a domain controller, and confirm domain controllers reachable from any PaperCut host are patched against the 2021 noPac flaws (CVE-2021-42278/CVE-2021-42287); GreyNoise reports the AI-orchestrated campaign reaching full domain admin through these paths in as little as five minutes after initial access.

alerts.headline: A pre-auth RCE chain in PaperCut NG/MF was exploited before any patch existed; tested maintenance releases now replace three emergency patches
alerts.summary: PaperCut NG and PaperCut MF (all versions) carry an unauthenticated remote-code-execution chain, CVE-2026-81578 (auth bypass, CVSS4.0 8.8) and CVE-2026-82078 (unsafe dynamic class loading, CVSS4.0 9.4), that PaperCut confirmed under active exploitation on 2026-08-27, before any CVE or patch existed. Fully tested maintenance releases 26.0.5, 25.0.13 and 24.1.10 (10 September 2026) replace the emergency patches and are the vendor's recommended build (the September bulletin, revised 2026-10-13, now names 24.1.11 for v24); servers still on Emergency Patch Release 1 or 2 need to upgrade now. There is no fix for v23 and earlier, and Huntress estimated on 28 August that 47% of the PaperCut installs it tracks ran v23 or older. GreyNoise now documents an AI-agent-orchestrated mass-exploitation campaign against this same chain, compromising at least 440 instances across 395 identified organizations since 31 August 2026, reaching full domain admin in as little as five minutes via legacy Active Directory escalation paths. watchTowr's write-up of 2026-10-09 shows the 28 August emergency build could still be taken without authentication through the Setup Wizard forms, and names CVE-2026-82077, an administrator-only Scan-to-Fax code-execution flaw that the vendor lists as fixed in 26.0.5, 25.0.13 and 24.1.10. Hunt.io's recovery of the attacker's open directories (2026-10-15) adds a second route to code execution through PaperCut's XML-RPC API, usable when its address allowlist is too permissive or no explicit token is set, a cron-kept reverse SOCKS tunnel, and live pivots into 45 victims, with Switzerland among the countries listed.

updates.summary: PaperCut shipped Emergency Patch Release 3 on 1 September 2026, superseding Release 2 and fixing two regressions Release 2 had introduced (broken SAML login; lost legacy Microsoft SQL Server driver support for external card lookup). PaperCut also confirms a second, more sophisticated wave of attacks against still-unpatched, internet-facing servers, and separately published incident data naming a post-compromise chain installing a SimpleHelp remote-access service and AnyDesk for durable access.

GreyNoise documents an AI-agent-orchestrated mass-exploitation campaign against this chain beginning 31 August 2026, using hundreds of AI agents to opportunistically compromise 440 PaperCut instances across 395 organizations in 48 countries, reaching domain admin against 12 of them in as little as five minutes via LSASS credential harvesting, the 2021 noPac flaws, or a PaperCut host running on the domain controller itself, all finishing with a DCSync-based NTDS.DIT credential dump.

PaperCut published fully tested maintenance releases 26.0.5, 25.0.13 and 24.1.10 on 10 September 2026. They carry every fix from the three emergency patches plus further hardening, and replace the emergency patches as the recommended build. A server on Emergency Patch Release 3 is protected and can schedule the move normally; one on Release 1 or 2 should upgrade now. There is still no fix for v23 and earlier. PaperCut also reports that new compromises slowed considerably in early September while unpatched, exposed servers are still targeted. CISA added both CVEs to its KEV catalog on 2026-08-31, which the status fields now record.

watchTowr published on 2026-10-09 how the emergency patches were bypassed in turn: the 28 August emergency build could still be taken without authentication through the Setup Wizard forms, and a new administrator-only Scan-to-Fax code-execution flaw, CVE-2026-82077, is fixed only in 26.0.5 and 25.0.13, not in the emergency builds. No source names exploitation of either, though PaperCut says Emergency Patch Release 3 closes off further attack vectors it has seen exploited. Earlier statements the cited sources do not support were corrected where they stood: the 2023 precedent, the university-customer statement, the emergency-patch chronology and the detection wording.

Hunt.io recovered the attacker's open directories (2026-10-15) and reports a second route to code execution through PaperCut's XML-RPC API that does not use the Tapestry bypass and works when the API allowlist is too permissive or no explicit token is set, a cron-kept reverse SOCKS tunnel, an offline LSA-secret playbook and 45 victims with live internal pivots, Switzerland among the countries listed. Hunt.io does not report the XML-RPC route used against a victim; PaperCut's documentation names the token and allowlist settings that close it. PaperCut's September bulletin, revised 2026-10-13, now lists CVE-2026-82077 as fixed in 24.1.10 and names 24.1.11 as the v24 build.

Corrects four statements: PaperCut says only that Emergency Patch Release 3 addresses two known regressions, not that Release 2 introduced them (the record of 2026-09-03 says it did); the web-log hunt now covers the LogonMessage route watchTowr documents and is cited; Huntress's 47% figure is dated to 28 August; and GreyNoise's twelve domain-admin victims are its count at last observation, not a final tally out of 395. The attacker-chosen Derby database name is removed from the detection text and the action as an indicator value.

alerts.headline: An attacker can reconstruct admin credentials for an exposed refrigeration controller offline, then silently disable cooling while the display reports normal
alerts.summary: Claroty Team82 disclosed 23 vulnerabilities (21 high) in Copeland XWEB300D/500D/500B PRO supervisory refrigeration controllers. Three chain to unauthenticated root RCE: an auth-bypass logic flaw in the Lua authentication handler, a deterministic admin-password generator derivable offline from the device's MAC address and current date, and an unauthenticated OS command injection via the libraries installation route. 18 further, authenticated-only command-injection flaws score CVSS 8.0 each, and CISA's advisory adds two low-severity unauthenticated flaws. Copeland fixed all 23 in firmware v1.13; no source read reports exploitation of these flaws, but CERT-FR's alert of 2026-10-13 now reports numerous compromises of Copeland xweb refrigeration controllers without naming models, flaws or the entry vector.

updates.summary: This entry stated that CVE-2026-21718 is the deterministic admin-password flaw. Claroty does not say that. Its per-CVE table text for that identifier is generic ("an authentication bypass vulnerability... enabling any attackers to bypass the authentication requirement and achieve pre-authenticated code execution", CVSS v3 10.0), and the narrative section that describes the MAC-address-and-date key derivation names no CVE id at all. The binding was an inference by elimination rather than a stated attribution, and a defender tracing the identifier to a patch note would have been misled. The mechanism description stands as reported; the id binding is removed from the title-adjacent claim, the CVE record's affected text, the body and the action, and the sourcing note now states what Claroty does and does not attribute.

CERT-FR revised its refrigeration-controller alert on 2026-10-13 to say it knows of numerous compromises of Copeland xweb controllers, in addition to Danfoss and Dixell units; it names no models, flaws or entry vector, so the earlier 'no exploitation reported' no longer describes the product family.

CISA's ICS advisory ICSA-26-057-10, which this entry said could not be located, lists all 23 identifiers: three missing ones are added (CVE-2026-3037, CVE-2026-22877, CVE-2026-20797), CVE-2026-21718 is typed as the authentication bypass both sources call it, the field-controller link and the register-map wording follow Claroty, the 'zero interaction' claim and the energy sector, which no source supports, are removed, the sourcing note records CISA's CWE for CVE-2026-21718, and the entry is now two-source.

actions: Find every Danfoss AK-SM and AK-SC, Copeland xweb and Dixell xweb refrigeration controller in facilities you own or that a contractor manages for you and take its management interface off the internet now, restoring access only through a secure VPN or protected network (filtering to the contractor's source addresses is an emergency stop-gap, and CERT-FR asks you to check your insurance conditions before cutting the contractor's data uplink); an end-of-life unit that gets no fixes needs replacing, because a factory reset leaves it vulnerable and probably compromised again.

On every such controller that was reachable from the internet, check the whole configuration, defrost ranges included, against the intended one; for a Danfoss unit that may have been taken over, restart it or otherwise factory-reset it, restore access only through a secure VPN or protected network and reconfigure it for service, then update its firmware, set the security level to Strict and change the default passwords, and on every Copeland or Dixell XWEB unit confirm the factory Admin password was changed and give each contractor a named account with an expiry date.
alerts.headline: CERT-FR adds Copeland and Dixell xweb to the hijacked refrigeration controllers; NCSC.ch rates the attacks exploited
alerts.summary: Coopérative U, Intermarché and E. Leclerc confirmed to AFP a cyberattack on their refrigeration systems overnight on 11 to 12 October 2026, which BFMTV reports as a remotely forced defrost at hundreds of stores. CERT-FR's alert, last revised on 2026-10-16, reports numerous compromises of Danfoss AK-SM and AK-SC controllers and of Copeland xweb and Dixell xweb, says campaigns are probably still running and that a factory reset alone does not protect an unpatched end-of-life unit, and in its current text tells owners to check the whole configuration, defrost ranges included, and to restart or otherwise factory-reset a compromised Danfoss unit. NCSC Switzerland rates the activity actively exploited, and Copeland's own bulletin of 14 October, carried in a Dixell France guide that CERT-FR links, acknowledges a vulnerability on a discontinued, end-of-life generation of XWEB EVO controllers and says to remove every XWEB EVO from the public internet at once. Danfoss says most affected units are legacy products or current AK-SM800A units on outdated firmware; no source names an actor, the flaw or how the attackers got in, and the Paris prosecutor is investigating.

updates.summary: CERT-FR revised its alert on 2026-10-13 to add Copeland xweb and Dixell xweb to the compromised controllers, says campaigns are probably still running, and says a factory reset alone is insufficient on an unpatched end-of-life unit. NCSC Switzerland published an advisory rating the activity actively exploited and naming the current AK-SM 800A on outdated firmware, and Danfoss says that is the case for the affected current units. Blick reports that Migros uses the same Danfoss systems in a limited number of Swiss stores and sees no sign they were targeted.

Censys's exposure report of 2026-10-14 points to three published 2025 AK-SM 800A flaws that Danfoss patched more than a year earlier and gives their firmware boundaries (4.3.1 or later fixes all three; Danfoss has not confirmed the vector), and shows exposed French controllers falling about 71 percent in three days with patched and unpatched builds leaving at the same rate, which Censys reads as operators taking units offline rather than patching.

CERT-FR's alert has a third version dated 2026-10-16 whose guidance differs for compromised and uncompromised units: the whole configuration, defrost ranges included, is to be checked, and a compromised Danfoss unit is to be restarted or otherwise factory-reset and reconfigured, with a caution to check insurance conditions before cutting the contractor's data uplink. The Dixell France operator guide that the alert links says any XWEB PRO on firmware 1.12.1 or earlier must be updated without delay, that XWEB units ship with a factory Admin account, and that remote access must go through an encrypted VPN; neither document names an entry vector.

The Dixell France guide that CERT-FR links was replaced on 2026-10-18 and now carries Copeland's own bulletin of 14 October 2026, which acknowledges the vulnerability on a discontinued, end-of-life generation of XWEB EVO controllers, says to remove every XWEB EVO from the public internet at once, gives a restore procedure and says to check product temperatures in the cabinets directly; the earlier statements about XWEB PRO firmware 1.12.1, a CISA advisory and a March 2024 bulletin are no longer on that page and are removed. Le Monde's report that the defrost operation was lengthened from one hour to eight so that alarms trigger late, and SecurityWeek's figure of about 700 supermarkets, the prosecutor's report of fires and the absence of a claim or ransom demand, are added, with Cybersecurity Dive's report that Copeland confirmed the flaw was found in discontinued controllers.

Two honeypot operators report exploitation attempts against the flaw, Defused from 2026-10-08 and Previdian from 2026-10-09, and NCSC Switzerland recorded it as actively exploited on 2026-10-12, without anyone establishing that an attempt would have compromised a system; SonicWall's advisory still says it has no evidence of exploitation. The two earlier unauthenticated Work Place SSRF flaws this year were exploited, each paired with an administrator-only command-execution flaw.

updates.summary: Previdian, a honeypot operator, reported exploitation attempts against CVE-2026-102255 on 2026-10-09, three days after the patch: crafted OPTIONS requests to the Work Place interface that try to reach the appliance's internal CouchDB service. Previdian has not established whether any attempt would have compromised a system, and SonicWall's advisory still says it has no evidence of exploitation.

NCSC Switzerland edited its advisory on 2026-10-12 to record the flaw as actively exploited, citing two honeypot operators: Defused, which saw attempts against its decoys from 2026-10-08, and Previdian, from 2026-10-09 (135 attempts from two US addresses). Previdian has not established that an attempt would have compromised a system, and SonicWall's advisory still says it has no evidence of exploitation.

The 2026-10-10 update attributed a count of 135 attempts from two addresses between 9 and 10 October to Previdian's page. The page carries no such window: the 135 attempts from two US addresses is the count The Hacker News relayed on 2026-10-12, and Previdian's page now shows 1,887 attempts from five addresses between 9 and 16 October.

alerts.headline: Ahsay admits its earlier AhsayCBS patches were incomplete; the hotfixes are partner-only and CISA lists both flaws as exploited
alerts.summary: Huntress observed from 2026-10-07 23:20 UTC attackers chaining two AhsayCBS flaws, CVE-2026-105133 (authentication bypass) and CVE-2026-105134 (code execution as SYSTEM through the Replication Receiver API), against internet-exposed servers of the backup management console that managed service providers and system integrators mainly use, dropping JSP webshells and an XMRig cryptominer; Bitdefender MDR investigated three intrusions through the same chain, and CISA added both flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-14. Ahsay now says its earlier patches v9.15.2.59 and v10.3.4.0 did not fully address the flaws, so servers on them are still exposed; the fixes are the hotfixes v10.3.4.45 (v10) and v9.15.2.70 (v7, v8 and v9), available only to partners with a portal login, and a server that was reachable before the hotfix needs a compromise check.

updates.summary: Ahsay says its previous patches v9.15.2.59 and v10.3.4.0 did not fully fix the flaws and names the hotfixes v10.3.4.45 and v9.15.2.70, available only to partners; Huntress verified the v10 hotfix, CISA added both flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-14, and Bitdefender MDR describes three intrusions through the chain. Hotfixes now cover v10 and v7 to v9, through the partner portal.

Horizon3.ai's source-level analysis of 2026-10-14 gives the root cause of both flaws (a caller-set flag that skips the administrator credential check, and an upload path that escapes the folder denylist), shows the chain runs as root on Linux, and lists server-side hunt artifacts: new .jsp files in served application directories, replication receivers created outside a change window, unexpected system administrator accounts, and requests carrying the bypass field or the receiver upload headers.
